title: Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry Fellowship
level: Clinical physician subspecialty fellowship; independent self-study curriculum (not a fellowship programme)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.intendedLevel: Postgraduate learner with psychiatry residency-level knowledge; physicians considering C-L fellowship or psychiatrists studying the subspecialty.
requiredPreparation: Medical-school-level human physiology, pharmacology and clinical reasoning.
Psychiatry residency knowledge of psychiatric interview, mental-status examination, psychopharmacology, DSM/ICD concepts, safety assessment and medical differential.
Ability to read clinical guidelines and distinguish source evidence from inference.
prerequisites.limitations: Self-study is not a substitute for an MD/DO, accredited general psychiatry residency, supervised fellowship, clinical encounter, competence assessment, hospital credentialing or board eligibility.

objectives: Clarify and answer consultation questions with collaborative, patient-centered communication.
Formulate psychiatric presentations in medically ill patients using time course, baseline, examination, collateral, medications and medical/neurological differential.
Recognize and reason about delirium, cognitive disorders, catatonia, medication syndromes and psychiatric complications of medical treatments.
Discuss decision-specific capacity, consent, suicidality, agitation and ethical/systems considerations with jurisdictional caution.
Use medication-safety reasoning, specialty collaboration, evidence appraisal and quality improvement without issuing unsupported treatment directives.
Explain the ABPN C-L subspecialty examination pathway and limits of course completion.

units.title: C-L Psychiatry as consultation, liaison and integrated service
objectives: Distinguish consultation from liaison/system-level work and identify both patient- and consultee-centered questions.
Reframe a vague referral into an answerable consult question, identify urgency and communicate a concise biopsychosocial formulation.
Describe service-level models including inpatient, outpatient, primary-care integration, e-consult and proactive consultation.
topics: Subspecialty definition and limits
Clarifying requests, chart review and collateral
Consultant-consultee alliance, team dynamics and follow-through
Equity, stigma and access
Models of care and service evaluation
boardDomains: ACGME patient care; interpersonal and communication skills; systems-based practice; professionalism (training domains, not a published exam blueprint)
units.casePractice: Use fictional one-line referral prompts to write a consult question, triage, and 3-sentence liaison response.
units.assessment: Submit structured consult acceptance/clarification note and a stakeholder map; rubric: question clarity 30%, formulation 30%, collaboration 20%, limits/safety 20%.

units.title: Medical-psychiatric assessment and formulation
objectives: Construct a time-anchored history, mental-status examination and risk assessment in context of medical illness.
Integrate physiology, medications/substances, baseline function, cognition, culture, trauma and social context without premature psychiatric attribution.
Create a prioritized differential and recommend questions for the primary team rather than issuing unsupported certainty.
topics: Baseline and collateral
Medical/neurological differential
Medication reconciliation and timeline
Communication across disciplines
Documenting uncertainty and patient preferences
boardDomains: ACGME patient care/medical knowledge; professionalism; communication
units.casePractice: Map competing explanations for acute behavioral change using a fictional admission timeline; never practice from actual patient records.
units.assessment: Graded formulation with evidence for/against at least three differential diagnoses, missing data and safety priorities.

units.title: Delirium, cognition and neuropsychiatry in hospital
objectives: Recognize acute/fluctuating attention and awareness change and distinguish screening from diagnosis.
Develop an etiologic differential, review contributors and communicate prevention/supportive care principles.
Recognize hypoactive presentations and assess baseline cognition; identify when neurological assessment/escalation is needed.
topics: Risk and recognition
Delirium phenomenology and tools
Medical, medication and substance contributors
Dementia and delirium overlap
Prevention, environment, family and transitions
units.casePractice: Compare a fictional fluctuating inattentive patient with a published delirium/catatonia case by link only; identify overlapping findings and missing medical workup.
units.assessment: Differential-and-plan memo; must state that a positive screen is not a diagnosis and avoid equating agitation with delirium.

units.title: Catatonia and acute medication-related syndromes
objectives: Identify psychomotor signs that warrant structured catatonia assessment and a search for psychiatric, medical, neurological, medication and substance causes.
Differentiate, while allowing overlap, catatonia, delirium, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and serotonin toxicity.
Describe emergency escalation and monitoring principles without issuing patient-specific dosing instructions.
topics: Catatonia features and rating tools
Concurrent delirium/catatonia
Malignant catatonia and NMS
Serotonin toxicity, anticholinergic toxicity and differential
EEG/imaging/CSF decisions in context
boardDomains: ACGME psychiatric disorders due to medical illness/treatment; patient care; medical knowledge
units.casePractice: Use an open published case as a linked case discussion only; make a timeline and state alternative explanations before formulation.
units.assessment: Syndrome comparison table with red flags, differentials and escalation; no medication-dose recommendations.

units.title: Psychopharmacology across medical illness
objectives: Use medication reconciliation and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic reasoning to identify interaction, organ-function, QTc, bleeding, sedation and delirium risks.
Balance psychiatric symptoms, medical constraints, patient preferences and interactions with transplant/oncology treatments.
Present a monitoring question to the responsible medical/pharmacy team and verify current references.
topics: Drug-drug interactions and altered absorption
Renal/hepatic impairment, electrolytes and ECG/QTc
Steroids, immunosuppressants, analgesics and anti-infectives
Medication discontinuation/withdrawal
Shared decision-making and monitoring
boardDomains: ACGME psychiatric complications of medical treatments, medications, surgery, transplantation and other therapies
units.casePractice: Fictional medication-list exercise: mark items for reconciliation and pharmacist/primary-team review; no prescribing instruction.
units.assessment: Interaction-risk memo graded for mechanism, missing information, monitoring collaboration and explicit uncertainty.

units.title: Decision-making capacity, consent and treatment refusal
objectives: Explain capacity as decision- and time-specific and separate capacity assessment from global status or legal competency.
Assess understanding, appreciation, reasoning and communicating a choice with supports and reversible contributors addressed.
Describe ethical involvement of patient/surrogate and identify jurisdictional and institutional legal-policy limits.
topics: Capacity/consent distinctions
Communication accommodations
Delirium, psychosis and refusal
Surrogate decision-making and ethics resources
Treatment over objection: limits and escalation
boardDomains: ACGME professionalism, patient care, communication, systems-based practice
units.casePractice: Fictional patient refuses a recommended investigation; learners identify decision, information needed, capacity domains and next consults without declaring legal outcome.
units.assessment: Capacity worksheet: decision specificity 20%, supported interview 25%, four domains 30%, patient/surrogate rights 15%, jurisdictional caveat 10%.

units.title: Suicide risk, self-harm, agitation and behavioral plans in the medical setting
objectives: Perform a structured suicide-risk formulation that integrates acute/chronic risk and protective factors, intent, access, context and uncertainty.
Design collaborative, least-restrictive safety and communication plans with the medical team and local protocols.
Recognize agitation as a symptom requiring differential and safety response, not a diagnosis by itself.
topics: Risk assessment and documentation
Medical/iatrogenic causes of agitation
Nonpharmacologic de-escalation and environment
Behavioral plans and team distress
Restraint/safety standards and handoff
boardDomains: ACGME patient care, professionalism, communication, systems-based practice
units.casePractice: Fictional inpatient expresses passive death wish and has delirium risk: formulate risk, identify unknowns and define escalation/handoff.
units.assessment: Structured note and team briefing; no risk-score-only disposition, no guaranteed risk prediction.

units.title: Substance use, intoxication and withdrawal on medical services
objectives: Build a substance/medication timeline and distinguish potential intoxication, withdrawal, delirium and primary psychiatric illness.
Describe collaborative assessment for alcohol, sedative and opioid-related presentations and the need for setting-specific monitoring.
Use motivational and non-stigmatizing language and coordinate with addiction specialists and the primary team.
topics: Alcohol/sedative withdrawal differentials
Opioid withdrawal and buprenorphine consultation concepts
Stimulants and atypical presentations
Pain, stigma, trauma and harm reduction
Team handoff and escalation
boardDomains: ACGME substance-use disorders in general medical settings; psychiatric complications of medical illness
units.casePractice: Fictional medication/substance history exercise; identify uncertainty, toxicology/medical data and specialty support needed.
units.assessment: Timeline plus differential and communication plan; demonstrate non-stigmatizing language and safe escalation.

units.title: Reproductive and perinatal C-L psychiatry
objectives: Identify psychiatric presentations intersecting with pregnancy/postpartum and reproductive health and the need for coordinated medical/obstetric consultation.
Compare risk-benefit reasoning and shared decision-making without using simplistic medication-safety labels.
Recognize that assessment and resources are person-centered and sensitive to context and local standards.
topics: Perinatal depression, bipolar disorder and psychosis in medical settings
Medication risk communication
Obstetric collaboration and postpartum transitions
Reproductive loss and trauma-informed care
boardDomains: ACGME psychiatric disorders related to reproductive life
units.casePractice: Fictional antenatal consult: write questions for patient, obstetric team and pharmacist; do not make unreferenced prescribing claims.
units.assessment: Shared-decision summary with explicit balance of knowns/unknowns, values and consultation plan.

units.title: Pain, palliative psychiatry, somatic symptoms and distress
objectives: Distinguish pain-related psychological distress, demoralization, depression and somatic symptom presentations without dismissing physical symptoms.
Integrate goals of care, serious illness, communication, trauma and access to supportive/psychological care.
Develop a collaborative formulation that attends to function, meaning and patient values.
topics: Pain and psychiatric comorbidity
Demoralization, grief and serious illness
Somatic symptom and related disorders
Palliative care communication
Psychotherapy/supportive interventions in constrained medical settings
boardDomains: ACGME acute/chronic pain; somatic symptom disorders; professionalism and patient-centered care
units.casePractice: Fictional oncology admission with pain and distress; compare hypotheses and describe what additional medical and patient-centered data are required.
units.assessment: Biopsychosocial formulation graded for avoiding invalidation, diagnostic overreach and treatment overclaim.

units.title: Consultation across transplant, oncology, cardiac, renal, HIV and neurological care
objectives: Adapt psychiatric consultation to complex medical therapies and specialty contexts while preserving the primary team’s medical decision authority.
Identify high-risk interaction and cognitive/behavioral concerns and formulate questions for specialty teams.
Explain how transplant and oncology consultation differ from candidacy gatekeeping or decisions about access to treatment.
topics: Transplant continuum and post-transplant mood symptoms
Psycho-oncology
Cardiac and renal psychiatry
HIV/neuropsychiatry and neurological illness
Collaborative care and e-consult models
boardDomains: ACGME psychiatric complications of medical/surgical/neurological illness and treatment, including transplantation
units.casePractice: Review a linked transplant psychiatry guidance paper and the published transplant-related case resource; formulate questions, not eligibility or candidacy recommendations.
units.assessment: Cross-specialty consultation note with source checks and distinction between psychiatric assessment and transplant selection.

units.title: Service leadership, teaching, scholarship, quality and transitions
objectives: Design a service improvement question with process, outcome and balancing measures; distinguish association from causation.
Communicate recommendations in an actionable, respectful form and plan transitions/follow-up.
Summarize an evidence-based mini-teaching session and explain limits of generalizing one program’s curriculum to another.
topics: Service models and demand triage
Proactive C-L and integrated care
Quality/safety and measurement
Teaching, feedback and scholarship
Transitions, continuity, equity and workforce wellbeing
boardDomains: ACGME systems-based practice, practice-based learning/improvement, communication, professionalism, scholarship
units.casePractice: Fictional service redesign proposal; do not use quality-assurance records or identifiable operational data.
units.assessment: QI/teaching capstone rubric: relevance 20%, measures 25%, evidence 20%, equity/safety 20%, communication and limitations 15%.

assignment.title: Integrated consultation portfolio (fictional cases only)
tasks: Clarify one intentionally vague referral and write a concise consult question and response plan.
Create a timeline-based biopsychosocial formulation for a fictional medically ill patient with at least three differential explanations.
Complete a decision-specific capacity worksheet or delirium/catatonia differential map, explicitly documenting missing data and local-policy questions.
Review one ACLP how-to guide and one primary source; submit a brief evidence appraisal distinguishing guideline, expert consensus, observational evidence and local rule.
Propose a C-L service improvement question with process, outcome and balancing measures; use no identifiable records or confidential QA material.
assignment.passingRule: Educational formative rubric only, not validated, not a board predictor and not evidence of clinical competence.

formative: Weekly retrieval questions tied to units
Short case formulations with explicit differential
Peer feedback on one-minute consult response
summative: Integrated consultation portfolio scored with rubric above
assessment.interpretation: No assessment in this independent course is validated as ABPN exam content or predictive of passing. No patient-care decision should be based on this assessment.

studyHours.planBreakdown: 36-hour video goal (only 2.6364 hours currently verified and free-viewable; 33.3636-hour gap), 30 hours source reading/case appraisal, 16 hours assignments and synthesis, 8 hours retrieval practice. This is a learner planning estimate, not observed training or clinical practice time.

mapping.name: Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page identifies an ACGME-accredited one-year PGY5 physician programme for psychiatrists, with two community hospitals, integrated primary care, e-consultation and additional reproductive psychiatry, palliative care and substance-use exposure; an academic project is mentored. The separate curriculum page names Cambridge Hospital, Everett Hospital and CHA primary-care clinics; weekly C-L seminar, monthly C-L/geriatric and integrated-care sessions, daily rounds and supervision. Public pages do not provide all rotation hours or case volume.

topicGaps: 23.3031 verified free specialty-video hours remain below the 36-hour floor (36,218 seconds of newly listed recordings added, 10.0606 hours). The target remains unmet; authored scripts and production targets do not count as media.

Focused published instruction is now available for delirium research appraisal, critical-care psychiatry, catatonia, acute benzodiazepine withdrawal, hospital opioid-use-disorder care, perinatal risk communication, selected medically complex consultations, QT risk and non-cardiac chest-pain formulation. These do not provide comprehensive, current guidance for those domains.

Still thin as full recorded instruction: decision-specific capacity and consent; broad consultation formulation and medical differential; suicide-risk assessment; agitation across settings; comprehensive psychopharmacology in renal/hepatic/transplant/oncology contexts; palliative psychiatry and pain; reproductive psychiatry beyond one medication-risk case; and service scholarship/quality improvement.

The public ACLP selection comprises many short recordings and four longer annual-meeting sessions, but the broader webinar archive is explicitly member-access. The current ACGME requirements remain a training-domain map, not a formal ABPN exam blueprint; no separate public ABPN C-L exam content outline was located.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardStatus.specialtyIdentity: Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry is a distinct physician subspecialty fellowship. ACGME defines the discipline across psychiatric conditions in medically, surgically, obstetrically and neurologically ill patients. Johns Hopkins and CHA each publish a one-year physician fellowship; this is not a generic research/non-physician directory category.
boardStatus.institutionVariants: The packet’s two official clinical variants are preserved separately: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine and Cambridge Health Alliance in a Harvard Medical School teaching-hospital context. Their public site details differ; no equivalence of rotations, capacity or outcomes is inferred.
boardStatus.boardExam: ABPN publishes a separate C-L Psychiatry subspecialty initial certification examination (the former psychosomatic-medicine subspecialty name changed January 1, 2018).

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A hospitalized adult develops acute, fluctuating inattention and disorientation after several days of medical illness. Which conceptual distinction is most important when interpreting a bedside screening result?

options.text: A positive delirium screen establishes a psychiatric diagnosis and rules out a neurological cause.
A screening result supports further clinical evaluation; delirium is a clinical syndrome requiring assessment for underlying causes.
A normal orientation question rules out delirium.
Agitation is required for delirium.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening is not diagnosis. Acute attention/awareness change requires clinical evaluation and review of potential causes; delirium may be hypoactive and may coexist with other conditions.

practiceQuestions.stem: A medically ill patient shows mutism, negativism and posturing with fluctuating attention. Which next reasoning step best reflects current source guidance?

options.text: Assume a primary psychotic disorder because catatonia and delirium cannot coexist.
Consider overlapping catatonia and delirium, use a structured examination and assess medical, neurologic, medication and substance causes.
Exclude catatonia because the patient is medically hospitalized.
Conclude catatonia from a single motor sign without further evaluation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: APA resource and published case material note phenotypic overlap and possible coexistence. A structured exam and evaluation for underlying causes are appropriate; this question does not prescribe therapy.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient refuses a proposed procedure. Which statement is the best starting point for a consultation-liaison capacity assessment?

options.text: Capacity is global and can be inferred from diagnosis.
Capacity is decision- and time-specific; support the patient’s participation and evaluate the relevant abilities, while checking applicable policy/law.
A family member’s disagreement proves incapacity.
Capacity and legal competency are interchangeable clinical terms.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Ethical and clinical assessment is specific to a particular decision and must support the person’s participation. AMA ethics guidance is not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific law or institutional policy.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a transplant recipient with depressive symptoms, what is the safest educational principle for medication review?

options.text: Select a psychotropic without consulting the medication list because the transplant team manages interactions.
Reconcile current and recently changed medications, assess organ function and interaction risks, and coordinate with the transplant/pharmacy team.
Assume all antidepressants are contraindicated after transplant.
Use a screening score alone to make a diagnosis and start treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Transplant recipients may have complex regimens and medical comorbidity. ACLP guidance emphasizes individualized evaluation and drug-interaction review; screen scores alone do not diagnose.

practiceQuestions.stem: A referring clinician sends “patient acting strangely—please see” for a medically unstable inpatient. What is the best first service response?

options.text: Reject the referral because it has no diagnosis.
Clarify the clinical question and urgency with the team, review immediate safety/medical context and define a focused assessment.
Assign a primary psychiatric diagnosis before meeting the patient.
Send a standard medication recommendation without patient evaluation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Consultation requires clarifying the consultee’s need, triaging safety and integrating the medical context. A vague request is an opportunity for collaborative reformulation, not premature diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees agitation in a hospital note and labels the presentation delirium. Which additional finding would most directly support a delirium formulation?

options.text: A stable, months-long pattern of social withdrawal alone.
Acute change from baseline with impaired attention/awareness and fluctuation in the setting of illness or toxic exposure.
One elevated symptom checklist score without clinical interview.
A remote psychiatric diagnosis by itself.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The time course and core attention/awareness disturbance are central features; assess contributors and competing diagnoses. Agitation or a history alone is insufficient.

practiceQuestions.stem: When a patient lacks decision-making capacity for a specific choice, what is the ethical approach described by AMA Opinion 2.1.2?

options.text: Exclude the patient from all discussion and let the attending choose.
Continue involving the patient as much as possible, identify an appropriate surrogate and support substituted judgment or best-interest reasoning as applicable.
Ask any available relative to make decisions regardless of law or policy.
Treat psychiatric consultation as authorization for involuntary treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AMA guidance emphasizes continued patient involvement, appropriate surrogate identification and principled decision support; applicable law and institutional policy remain essential.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a first presentation of catatonic signs during acute medical illness, which approach is most aligned with the APA resource document?

options.text: Assume it is psychiatric and avoid medical testing.
Perform a thorough clinical evaluation, review medication/substance changes and consider neurologic causes; tailor tests to the clinical picture.
Order every possible neurodiagnostic test irrespective of clinical context.
Use an imaging abnormality alone to establish catatonia.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The APA resource recommends a thorough evaluation informed by clinical context, including medical, neurological, medication and substance causes; excessive testing also carries harms and should be individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A C-L team wants to improve early consultation on a medical ward. Which measurement plan is most defensible?

options.text: Use a single favorable outcome and assume the intervention caused it.
Define the target population and workflow, then track process, outcome and balancing measures while accounting for confounding.
Count consultations only and infer improved patient outcomes.
Use identifiable QA cases for course publication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A service change needs transparent measures and attention to unintended consequences; observed associations do not establish causality, and confidential QA/patient material should not be exposed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the board pathway associated with this course’s specialty?

options.text: A C-L course completion confers eligibility to practice as a subspecialist.

ABPN lists a separate Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry subspecialty examination; its published criteria include general psychiatry certification and one year of ACGME-accredited C-L fellowship training, subject to current policies.
A general psychiatry residency’s C-L rotation alone replaces the fellowship year.
Every institution variant has a separate board examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPN publishes a C-L Psychiatry subspecialty exam and specific training prerequisites. Self-study does not satisfy them or confer eligibility/certification. The institution programmes are not separate boards.

assignment.title: Integrated fictional consultation portfolio
deliverables: A problem representation and prioritized differential for two explicitly fictional vignettes
A source-dated guideline comparison and safety/assessment pathway map
A five-minute oral case presentation that names uncertainty, missing data, and consultation needs
A 500-word evidence appraisal of one public grand-round talk versus current official guidance
assignment.rubric: Clinical reasoning 30%; source and date accuracy 25%; safety/uncertainty 20%; communication/cultural humility 15%; privacy and attribution 10%. Must identify all cases as fictional; no real patient material. This is educational feedback, not clinical competency sign-off.

assessment.format: 12 unit checks (formative), original 10-question knowledge check, and portfolio rubric.
assessment.passingInterpretation: No passing threshold predicts ABPN outcomes. Suggested self-study completion: answer each rationale in own words, score ≥80% on a second attempt after remediation, and document sources used. Not a validated exam or credential.
assessment.questionBankStatus: Original educational items, not official ABPN questions.

studyHours.basis: Transparent learner study plan, not video time or clinical training: 12 units × 8 h (96); portfolio, source reading and case discussion (48); spaced retrieval/remediation (36). Adapt as needed; no competency is certified.

topicGaps: The hour floor is met by 101 distinct public playlist entries (metadata total, unique video IDs), but this is a Grand Rounds archive, not a systematic 36-hour didactic course. Titles and runtime cannot establish complete blueprint coverage or evidence currency.

Some ABPN topics are likely underrepresented in counted recordings, including structured diagnosis/differential, psychopharmacology safety, personality disorders, sleep, sexual/paraphilic disorders, legal/ethical detail, examination/neurology, and full practice-based learning. Follow current blueprint and readings.

boardNames: American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) — Psychiatry Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: A distinct ABPN initial certification examination exists for core Psychiatry; official 2025 content specifications were used. This is not a subspecialty fellowship curriculum. The named Hopkins program is an institutional residency. ACGME’s public specialty page provides current requirements, but program-specific accreditation status was not independently verified in ACGME ADS; do not treat institutional listing as status confirmation.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: No course enrollment or assessment confers medical training, ACGME residency completion, clinical-skills evaluations, an unrestricted license, board eligibility, or certification. ABPN determines eligibility. Its current requirements describe a full PGY-1 followed by three full years of psychiatry residency under specified accepted training patterns, 12 continuous outpatient months, three clinical-skills evaluations, and licensing conditions; check the ABPN source directly for the applicable pathway and current rules.

officialProgrammes.name: General Psychiatry Residency Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The item-packet URL resolves to Hopkins residency routing; the current official psychiatry site describes the Johns Hopkins Hospital Residency in Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, its PGY-1–4 structure, supervised clinical rotations, didactics, and 2024–25 prospectus. Public pages do not disclose a complete syllabus/hour ledger. The packet names one general psychiatry residency. Multiple application entry pathways are not separate tracks. No combined programme or board exam is inferred. Clinical/research postdoctoral fellowships listed by the department are not additional physician residencies.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Only the exact Johns Hopkins General Psychiatry Residency named in the packet is included. Other institutional variants were not silently merged into this item. The department separately lists clinical/research postdoctoral opportunities; no such supplement is represented as a physician residency. No separate child/adolescent track, combined programme, or non-physician track is added.
sourceCaveats: The Hopkins programme site confirms its programme identity and publicly described curricular structure, not program-specific ACGME status; ADS verification was not performed.
ABPN rules change; follow the board’s current route-specific conditions. The 2025 content specifications are a guide, not exhaustive or predictive of any examination.

The lecture ledger records playlist metadata duration, not independently measured playback. The list is public; a media player/access test was not conducted for every item. No duplicates by canonical YouTube video ID; short entries excluded.
NICE recommendations are jurisdiction-specific; medication warnings and current local rules must be checked. The syllabus makes no patient-specific recommendations.
Published case links are for source reading only. Verify each article’s consent/de-identification statement and license before class reuse; no images or patient records are copied.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 23-year-old reports 3 weeks of auditory hallucinations and declining function. Which next step best reflects sound initial reasoning?

options.text: Assume schizophrenia and begin a fixed treatment plan without further history
Clarify symptom chronology, mood/substance/medical context, risk, collateral, and examination before refining the differential
Treat a single hallucination as proof of a primary psychotic disorder
Use a screening scale as the sole diagnostic assessment

practiceQuestions.rationale: Psychosis requires a clinical assessment and differential; duration and context matter, and medical/substance and mood explanations should be considered. A course cannot determine an individual diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient screening positive on the ASQ should next receive which action according to NIMH pathway principles?

options.text: Treat the screening result as a definitive prediction of suicide
A brief suicide safety assessment by a trained clinician to guide disposition
No further assessment if the patient denies depression
Automatic psychiatric admission in every positive case

practiceQuestions.rationale: NIMH describes positive screening followed by a brief clinician-led safety assessment to determine the next step; the screen itself is not a disposition.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes screening from diagnosis?

options.text: A validated screen can identify who needs further assessment but is not by itself a full diagnosis
A positive screen confirms a specific disorder
A negative screen overrides clinical concern
Screening removes need for context-specific evaluation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening tools identify people who may need additional assessment; the clinical context and pathway still matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: When considering a bipolar-spectrum formulation, which information is especially important?

options.text: Only the current mood-state score
Longitudinal history of mood episodes, duration, change from baseline, impairment, and possible substance/medical contributors
Family history alone is diagnostic
Response to one antidepressant proves bipolar disorder

practiceQuestions.rationale: Assessment is longitudinal and contextual; NICE guidance covers recognizing and assessing suspected bipolar disorder and differentiating mood states.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which course claim is justified by the Johns Hopkins public curriculum page?

options.text: This self-study grants the same supervised clinical experience
The official residency combines didactics with supervised clinical experiences across PGY years
The public webpage publishes every hour and every lecture
Enrolling in this independent course confers Hopkins affiliation

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official page describes supervised clinical experience and didactics, but not a complete syllabus; the independent course confers none of those clinical experiences.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the correct relationship between ABPN certification and this independent course?

options.text: Course completion establishes ABPN eligibility
ABPN eligibility requires specified medical training, clinical skills and licensure conditions; the board determines eligibility
A course exam substitutes for clinical skills evaluations
A course certificate guarantees passing the exam

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPN defines formal prerequisites, including training and clinical skills requirements. Independent study does not satisfy them or predict passing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which structure best represents ABPN’s psychiatry exam blueprint?

options.text: Only diagnoses in one dimension
Disorders/topics crossed with physician competencies/mechanisms
A score weighted only to medication selection
A rotation checklist

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current content specifications explicitly use two interrelated dimensions: disorders/topics and competencies/mechanisms.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinical education video is public to watch. Which reuse approach is appropriate?

options.text: Download and redistribute slides by default
Link to the source and check recording/slide license and permissions before copying or editing
Assume YouTube availability transfers copyright
Copy any patient images because names are omitted

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free public viewing does not grant republication or image rights. This course links original public videos only; no copied media or patient imagery.

practiceQuestions.stem: When teaching antipsychotic guidance, which practice is most defensible?

options.text: Use an old lecture as the sole authority
Check current guideline text, dates, patient context, monitoring and safety qualifiers
Assume a grand-round talk is universally applicable
Treat guidelines as overrides to individual clinical judgment

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guidance changes; NICE CG178 was updated in 2026 and emphasizes recommendation context and individual needs. Supplement talks with current guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A published case report is considered for class discussion. What is the safe first step?

options.text: Copy all images and narrative into course notes
Link only; confirm author consent/de-identification and permissions before reuse, and do not add patient records
Treat publication as blanket permission for derivative use
Add identifying details to make the case realistic

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course only links published cases and does not reproduce protected details or images; case reuse and rights need explicit verification.

objectives: Assess late-life psychiatric presentations in developmental, cultural, medical, functional and environmental context.

Map topics to current ABPN and ACGME domains and appraise clinical claims by source, date, population and limitations.

topicGaps: Delirium is better mapped through current NICE CG103 recommendation sections and linked to one brief awareness video, but no additional verified full-length current specialist lecture was found; detailed differential, workup and longitudinal delirium management remain under-taught by recording.

Late-life depression now has one 6:33 public RCPsych awareness resource and new scripted teaching; bipolar-spectrum differential, treatment resistance, ECT/rTMS selection, suicide assessment, anxiety, trauma and prolonged grief lack a verified full-length specialist recording.

Neurocognitive etiologies (Lewy body/Parkinson, frontotemporal, mixed, TBI, rare syndromes), biomarker interpretation, anti-amyloid eligibility/safety and contemporary shared decisions still lack a verified comprehensive updated recording; check current FDA labels/guidelines before use.

Late-life psychosis, catatonia, sleep, alcohol/sedative/opioid use, pain, medical-psychiatric interfaces and geriatric psychopharmacology need dedicated current recordings; legacy dementia videos are conceptual only.

Capacity, consent, jurisdiction-specific law, safeguarding/elder abuse, palliative care, caregiver strain, home/PACE/nursing-home systems, care transitions, quality improvement and evidence appraisal lack verified full-length specialist recordings.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: An 82-year-old with established major neurocognitive disorder becomes inattentive and fluctuating over 36 hours after a medication change and reduced oral intake. What is the best next framing?

options.text: Treat as expected dementia progression
Urgently evaluate delirium and precipitating causes, including medication and medical contributors
Diagnose major depression based on withdrawal
Assume Lewy body dementia from fluctuation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute change and inattention/fluctuation support delirium as an urgent syndrome; dementia can coexist. Evaluate causes and safety rather than attributing to baseline disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: A brief cognitive screen is abnormal in a patient whose preferred language differs from the test language. Which response is best?

options.text: Declare dementia based on score
Repeat the same tool more loudly
Interpret cautiously and arrange culturally/language-appropriate comprehensive assessment including informant and function
Exclude cognition from evaluation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Brief screens do not diagnose dementia; language/cultural validity matters. A positive screen requires follow-up comprehensive evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has progressive cognitive complaints, but independent finances and medication management remain intact and collateral confirms little change from baseline. What is essential before distinguishing mild from major neurocognitive disorder?

options.text: Age alone
Functional impact and change from baseline
One MRI finding
Caregiver preference alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: The functional consequences and trajectory are central to syndrome-level distinction; no isolated scan or age determines diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: An older patient with depressive symptoms and a remote period of markedly reduced need for sleep and elevated energy is being considered for antidepressant monotherapy. What should be done first?

options.text: Start immediately without history
Clarify possible bipolar-spectrum history and assess current risk/medical contributors
Assume late-life depression excludes bipolarity
Use a screening score as a diagnosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: A careful longitudinal mood history and safety/medical assessment should precede treatment selection; avoid assuming unipolar disorder.

practiceQuestions.stem: A person with dementia has new agitation during bathing. No immediate danger is present. Which initial approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Escalate directly to a sedative
Assess pain, fear, environment, communication and unmet needs; adapt care and monitor
Confront the person about irrational behavior
Restrict all activity

practiceQuestions.rationale: Target unmet needs and modifiable triggers with person-centered nonpharmacologic measures first when safe; evaluate medical causes.

practiceQuestions.stem: An older adult with cognitive impairment has new falls and confusion shortly after a medication was added. What reasoning step is highest priority?

options.text: Assume inevitable neurodegeneration
Reconcile medication timeline and assess adverse effects/interactions alongside medical causes
Stop every medicine independently
Diagnose psychosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: Medication-related harm is an important reversible contributor; prompt clinician-led medication review and broader assessment are warranted.

practiceQuestions.stem: A caregiver says they can no longer safely support a relative at home. What should the clinician do?

options.text: Dismiss caregiver concerns
Assess caregiver distress and capacity, patient preferences/safety, and connect with an interdisciplinary/community plan
Promise that memory will recover
Share confidential information without considering consent

practiceQuestions.rationale: Caregiver assessment and support are core competencies; planning should integrate patient values, safety, lawful confidentiality and community resources.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees visual hallucinations, parkinsonism, and cognitive fluctuations in a patient. What is the safest conclusion?

options.text: This triad alone proves one diagnosis
Consider Lewy body disease in the differential, assess time course/other causes and medication sensitivity, and seek appropriate diagnostic evaluation
Start high-potency antipsychotic reflexively
Ignore hallucinations as normal aging

practiceQuestions.rationale: The pattern raises a diagnostic consideration but does not prove etiology; evaluate broadly and consider medication-related risks.

title: Psychosocial Oncology Fellowship Track
level: Clinical physician fellowship track (subspecialty training within Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry; not a standalone psycho-oncology board specialty)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Advanced postgraduate self-study for psychiatrists who have completed or are nearing adult psychiatry residency; not intended to qualify learners for independent patient care.
Foundational psychiatric interview, DSM-based differential, medical assessment, psychopharmacology and evidence appraisal.
Working knowledge of oncology treatment trajectories and interprofessional care; use current clinical references and local escalation protocols.
No patient-care privileges, supervision, or clinical case exposure is supplied.
objectives: Use a screening-to-assessment-to-referral-to-follow-up workflow without treating a screen as diagnosis.
Formulate cancer-related adjustment, anxiety, depressive, delirium, cognitive, existential and safety concerns with a medical differential.
Appraise guideline recommendations and their population/strength/limits; consult current primary sources.
Describe interprofessional coordination, consent, privacy, safety, documentation and quality improvement.
Explain the actual training/board boundary: C-L Psychiatry has an ABPN subspecialty exam; psycho-oncology itself does not have a separate exam identified.

units.title: Psychosocial oncology: scope, disease trajectory, and clinical role
objectives: Differentiate psychosocial distress, mental disorder, and social/spiritual need without pathologizing expected response.
Describe physician-led psycho-oncology within interprofessional cancer care.
Map needs and supports across diagnosis, treatment, surveillance, recurrence, survivorship, and end of life.
topics: Scope; trajectory; family and caregiver inclusion; access, equity, and stigma
Whole-person needs: symptoms, coping, practical barriers, social support and meaning are distinct but may coexist.
Service boundary: physician C-L psychiatry sits within oncology's interprofessional care; a screen does not define the role or diagnose.
Cancer trajectory mapping: diagnosis, active treatment, surveillance, recurrence, survivorship and serious illness can each change needs.
boardDomains: ACGME: patient care, knowledge, systems-based practice
ABPN general Psychiatry: psychosocial mechanisms; systems-based practice
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Written scope map and handoff: identify need, role, and appropriate referral; rubric 0-2 each for accuracy, boundaries, continuity.

units.title: Distress screening, assessment, triage, and follow-up
objectives: Explain the Distress Thermometer (DT) and Problem List as screening rather than diagnostic tests.
Use a positive screen to conduct a clinical interview and select appropriate second-stage measures.
Design closed-loop follow-up with responsibility, documentation, reassessment, and referral.
topics: Screen at new/clinically appropriate visits; DT≥4 in NCCN 2.2024 prompts follow-up—not diagnosis; dynamic triggers; no-score-alone treatment decisions
Workflow ownership: specify who reviews a score, who performs second-stage assessment, who makes each referral and who closes the loop.
A threshold is a workflow trigger, not a rule-out or diagnostic boundary; clinical concern can override a low score.
Measure pathway fidelity separately from outcomes: screening, follow-up/referral, time-to-contact and reassessment are process measures.
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Create workflow with ≥4 trigger points and named responder; rubric covers triage, referral match, follow-up, documentation, safety.

units.title: Adjustment, anxiety, and uncertainty
objectives: Differentiate expected distress/adjustment from anxiety disorder using duration, impairment, course, differential, and patient goals.
Assess symptom timing relative to tests, treatment, toxicity, and disease changes.
Communicate uncertainty using empathic, culturally and linguistically responsive language.
topics: Scanxiety; adjustment disorders; panic/GAD; illness uncertainty; medical causes and medication effects
Formulation dimensions: symptom onset, duration, frequency, functional impact, triggers, coping, patient goals and relevant medical/medication context.
Differentiate event-linked fear or uncertainty from persistent, generalized or impairing anxiety without labeling expected reactions as disorder.
Communication under uncertainty: acknowledge uncertainty, identify the next known step, and invite the patient's preferred support.
boardDomains: ACGME: response to illness, psychotherapeutic care
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Compare two fictional assessment plans; rubric: differential, function/time course, medical contributors, patient-centered formulation.

units.title: Depression, demoralization, grief, and suicide-risk response
objectives: Separate major depression from grief, adjustment, demoralization, fatigue, delirium, and treatment effects.
Assess suicidal thoughts directly and urgently escalate active/imminent risk using local protocols.
Describe evidence-informed psychological and pharmacologic options without protocolizing individual prescribing.
topics: Somatic symptom overlap; emotional-cognitive symptoms; hopelessness; desire for hastened death vs suicidal intent; safety and escalation
Separate emotional-cognitive depressive symptoms from fatigue, appetite, sleep and concentration changes that may have cancer/treatment causes.
Distinguish grief, adjustment, demoralization, desire for hastened death and suicidal intent by asking what words mean to the individual.
Direct suicide inquiry is paired with assessment of ideation, intent, plan, means, context and protective factors; use local urgent safety pathways when indicated.

units.assessment: Risk formulation from a fictional vignette; rubric: direct inquiry, intent/plan/means/protective context, medical team coordination, safety escalation.

units.title: Psychopharmacology in oncology and serious illness
objectives: Reconcile cancer therapies, supportive medications, substances, organ function, and psychiatric medicines before treatment selection.
Recognize interaction, QT, bleeding, metabolic, sedative, and delirium risks that require specialist review.
Frame medication decisions as individualized shared decisions subject to current references and pharmacist/oncology collaboration.
topics: Drug-drug interactions; CYP; QT risk; corticosteroid-related mood; antiemetic and opioid effects; organ dysfunction; medication review
Medication reconciliation as a systems task: antineoplastic agents, supportive drugs, psychiatric medicines, nonprescription products, substances, allergies, organ function and recent changes.
Interaction review: identify mechanism and clinical consequence, check current references and consult oncology/pharmacy; do not infer a safe drug choice from a static list.
Document uncertainty and monitoring/coordination responsibility; this curriculum contains no patient-specific medication orders or doses.
boardDomains: ACGME: psychoactive medicines in medical illness; interactions
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Interaction-analysis worksheet for fictional medication list; rubric: source/date, interaction mechanism, risk uncertainty, consultation/safety.

units.title: Delirium, cognition, and acute behavioral change
objectives: Recognize acute/fluctuating attention and cognition as a time-sensitive medical evaluation problem.
Prioritize precipitants and medication/toxic-metabolic contributors before assuming primary psychiatric illness.
Communicate a prioritized differential and nonpharmacologic safety measures to the oncology team.
topics: Delirium phenotypes; hypoactive delirium; medication effects; infection/metabolic/neurologic contributors; cognitive changes
Acute change reasoning: establish baseline, time course and fluctuation; assess attention/awareness and consider delirium before attributing new behavior to a primary psychiatric syndrome.
Prioritize review of medication/toxic-metabolic, infectious, neurologic and other medical precipitants with the treating team.
Hypoactive presentations and changes in sleep-wake behavior still warrant time-sensitive assessment; educational content is not a bedside protocol.
boardDomains: ACGME: delirium and medically caused psychiatric syndromes
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Differential and consultation note outline; rubric: syndrome recognition, reversible causes, safety, collaborative communication.

units.title: Psychotherapy and brief psychosocial interventions
objectives: Match intervention to symptoms, severity, preference, access, culture, and cancer context.
Summarize ASCO 2023 options for moderate/severe anxiety and depression while respecting recommendation qualifiers.
Use supportive, CBT/behavioral activation, problem-solving, meaning-centered, and caregiver-aware approaches conceptually.
topics: ASCO 2023 adult-survivor guideline; supportive care; CBT; BA; MBSR; interpersonal therapy; meaning and dignity; limits of generalization
Translate guideline recommendations into an applicability statement: population, symptom severity, intervention, evidence strength and access assumptions.
ASCO 2023 recommendations for anxiety/depression apply to adult cancer survivors from diagnosis onward; choices differ by moderate versus severe symptoms and are not a universal regimen.
For each intervention, state patient preference, language/culture, availability and a way to reassess benefit rather than assuming a modality works for every person.
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Evidence-to-treatment matrix with severity and access; rubric: guideline match, certainty, preference, referral and outcome measure.

units.title: Communication, family systems, and shared decisions
objectives: Conduct a brief empathic assessment with permission, open questions, validation, and agenda alignment.
Include family/caregivers only with consent and respect patient-defined supports.
Address treatment decision distress, uncertainty, and disagreement without coercion.
topics: Disclosure; serious news context; conflict; family dynamics; caregiver distress; decisional support
Start with permission, agenda-setting, reflective listening and validation; do not promise certainty not supported by oncology information.
Family/caregiver participation is patient-defined and consent-based; document who may receive information and what the patient wants shared.
When there is disagreement, separate medical facts, values, communication barriers and unresolved safety questions; avoid coercion.
boardDomains: ACGME: communication with medically ill patients and teams
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Role-play transcript analysis (fictional); rubric: agenda, empathy, consent/confidentiality, uncertainty, action plan.

units.title: Palliative care, existential distress, and end of life
objectives: Distinguish palliative care from hospice and frame psychiatric care in serious illness.
Assess suffering, demoralization, spiritual/existential distress, and desire for hastened death with nuanced inquiry.
Describe goals-of-care and capacity consultation roles while not substituting for local law or team process.
topics: Meaning, dignity, grief, existential concerns, capacity interface, interdisciplinary palliative services
Palliative care is interdisciplinary support for serious illness and is not synonymous with hospice; psychiatric consultation addresses a bounded question within team care.
Explore existential, spiritual and relational suffering in the patient's own language; a wish that suffering end requires clarification rather than assumption.
Capacity questions are decision-specific and jurisdiction-dependent; a psychiatric consultation does not replace the treating team's lawful process.
boardDomains: ACGME: palliative care and end-of-life; capacity
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Formulate a fictional values-sensitive consult; rubric: clarify construct, patient values, capacity question, team collaboration, boundaries.

units.title: Caregiver, family, survivorship, and late effects
objectives: Screen caregivers and survivors for mental health and practical needs at transitions.
Consider cognitive, sleep, sexual, relationship, work, financial, and recurrence-related concerns.
Build an equity-aware survivorship follow-up and referral plan.
topics: Caregiver distress; survivorship; late effects; fear of recurrence; socioeconomic stressors
Transition check-ins: treatment completion, surveillance, recurrence, late effects and caregiver-role changes can create new support needs.
Survivorship planning includes practical access, cognition, sleep, relationships, work, financial stress and fear of recurrence without assuming one standardized experience.
Caregiver screening is separate from patient assessment and follows the patient's consent/privacy preferences.
boardDomains: ACGME: social determinants and responses to illness
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Transition plan with follow-up triggers; rubric: caregiver consent, problem-specific referral, continuity, access/equity.

units.title: Interprofessional consultation and service design
objectives: Write a question-focused psychiatric consultation and clarify what the referring service needs.
Design closed-loop referrals across psychiatry, psychology, social work, chaplaincy, palliative care, and oncology.
Select process measures for screening-to-follow-up quality improvement without inferring clinical outcomes.
topics: Consultation formulation; service models; warm handoffs; referral; documentation; QI measures
Consultation formulation: translate the referral into a focused question, relevant time course, medical context, risks, requested decision and recommendations with a named owner.
Closed-loop referral: patient consent, service match, handoff, access barrier plan and confirmation of follow-up.
Quality-improvement denominators and measures must be prespecified and privacy-protected; a process change alone does not prove improved clinical outcomes.
boardDomains: ACGME: systems, teamwork, care transitions, PBLI
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: QI driver diagram and sample audit fields; rubric: meaningful process measure, ownership, safety, privacy.

units.title: Evidence appraisal, ethics, law, and professional practice
objectives: Appraise evidence strength, population, and applicability in psycho-oncology.
Explain privacy, consent, capacity, confidentiality, documentation, and jurisdictional variation.
Identify role limits, self-care, moral distress, and need for licensed supervision.
topics: Guideline currency; evidence hierarchy; consent and capacity; ethical/legal uncertainty; professional wellbeing; research/QI distinctions
Evidence appraisal: locate population, design, outcome, certainty, publication/version date and applicability before generalizing a recommendation.
Distinguish a clinical-program description, accreditation requirement and board-exam eligibility policy; each answers a different question.
Confidentiality, consent, capacity, research/QI distinctions and professional well-being require current institutional policy, jurisdictional law and supervision.
units.casePractice: Use fictional composite vignettes only for exercises. Follow linked published/de-identified clinical cases in place; do not copy/rehost patient details or images.
units.assessment: Appraise an open guideline and draft a scope/ethics statement; rubric: currency, methods, applicability, legal caution, supervision.

assignment.title: Psychosocial oncology consult-pathway case conference and QI plan
assignment.directions: Using the fictional case prompts in the units, submit a 1,200–1,800-word problem formulation and a one-page closed-loop referral pathway. Include symptom timeline, differential and medical contributors, safety/consent issues, patient priorities, service/referral match, owner and timing for follow-up, evidence citations with versions, and one auditable process measure. Do not write real-patient information or a medication order.

rubric.levels: 0 unsupported; 1 incomplete; 2 balanced with time course, function, context and medical differential.
0 no pathway; 1 referral only; 2 need-matched referral, named owner, timing and closure.
0 unsafe; 1 partial; 2 consent/privacy/safety, agency and boundaries addressed.
0 unsupported; 1 citations without applicability; 2 primary current sources, date/version and limits.
0 unclear; 1 generic; 2 actionable handoff and non-causal process metric.

assignment.passThreshold: For learning only, require ≥70% and no zero for safety; this is not an exam or clinical competence standard.

assessment.formative: 10 original single-best-answer questions with explanations; unit case/reflection exercises; source-appraisal worksheet.
assessment.summative: Course assignment graded against the rubric.
assessment.limitations: All 10 questions are original, educational and not official or leaked board items; every scenario is fictional. They do not predict exam performance or establish competence.

studyHours.plan: Study plan, not an observed time claim: 12 units × 3 hours reading/lesson work (36 h), assignment 6 h, practice questions and review 3 h; total planned learner study 45 hours. Video recording hours are tracked separately and currently zero verified.

unitMap.text: Psychosocial oncology: scope, disease trajectory, and clinical role
coveredTopics: Scope; trajectory; family and caregiver inclusion; access, equity, and stigma
Whole-person needs: symptoms, coping, practical barriers, social support and meaning are distinct but may coexist.
Service boundary: physician C-L psychiatry sits within oncology's interprofessional care; a screen does not define the role or diagnose.
Cancer trajectory mapping: diagnosis, active treatment, surveillance, recurrence, survivorship and serious illness can each change needs.

unitMap.text: Distress screening, assessment, triage, and follow-up
coveredTopics: Screen at new/clinically appropriate visits; DT≥4 in NCCN 2.2024 prompts follow-up—not diagnosis; dynamic triggers; no-score-alone treatment decisions
Workflow ownership: specify who reviews a score, who performs second-stage assessment, who makes each referral and who closes the loop.
A threshold is a workflow trigger, not a rule-out or diagnostic boundary; clinical concern can override a low score.
Measure pathway fidelity separately from outcomes: screening, follow-up/referral, time-to-contact and reassessment are process measures.

unitMap.text: Adjustment, anxiety, and uncertainty
coveredTopics: Scanxiety; adjustment disorders; panic/GAD; illness uncertainty; medical causes and medication effects
Formulation dimensions: symptom onset, duration, frequency, functional impact, triggers, coping, patient goals and relevant medical/medication context.
Differentiate event-linked fear or uncertainty from persistent, generalized or impairing anxiety without labeling expected reactions as disorder.
Communication under uncertainty: acknowledge uncertainty, identify the next known step, and invite the patient's preferred support.

unitMap.text: Depression, demoralization, grief, and suicide-risk response
coveredTopics: Somatic symptom overlap; emotional-cognitive symptoms; hopelessness; desire for hastened death vs suicidal intent; safety and escalation
Separate emotional-cognitive depressive symptoms from fatigue, appetite, sleep and concentration changes that may have cancer/treatment causes.
Distinguish grief, adjustment, demoralization, desire for hastened death and suicidal intent by asking what words mean to the individual.
Direct suicide inquiry is paired with assessment of ideation, intent, plan, means, context and protective factors; use local urgent safety pathways when indicated.

unitMap.text: Psychopharmacology in oncology and serious illness
coveredTopics: Drug-drug interactions; CYP; QT risk; corticosteroid-related mood; antiemetic and opioid effects; organ dysfunction; medication review
Medication reconciliation as a systems task: antineoplastic agents, supportive drugs, psychiatric medicines, nonprescription products, substances, allergies, organ function and recent changes.
Interaction review: identify mechanism and clinical consequence, check current references and consult oncology/pharmacy; do not infer a safe drug choice from a static list.
Document uncertainty and monitoring/coordination responsibility; this curriculum contains no patient-specific medication orders or doses.

unitMap.text: Delirium, cognition, and acute behavioral change
coveredTopics: Delirium phenotypes; hypoactive delirium; medication effects; infection/metabolic/neurologic contributors; cognitive changes
Acute change reasoning: establish baseline, time course and fluctuation; assess attention/awareness and consider delirium before attributing new behavior to a primary psychiatric syndrome.
Prioritize review of medication/toxic-metabolic, infectious, neurologic and other medical precipitants with the treating team.
Hypoactive presentations and changes in sleep-wake behavior still warrant time-sensitive assessment; educational content is not a bedside protocol.

unitMap.text: Psychotherapy and brief psychosocial interventions
coveredTopics: ASCO 2023 adult-survivor guideline; supportive care; CBT; BA; MBSR; interpersonal therapy; meaning and dignity; limits of generalization
Translate guideline recommendations into an applicability statement: population, symptom severity, intervention, evidence strength and access assumptions.
ASCO 2023 recommendations for anxiety/depression apply to adult cancer survivors from diagnosis onward; choices differ by moderate versus severe symptoms and are not a universal regimen.
For each intervention, state patient preference, language/culture, availability and a way to reassess benefit rather than assuming a modality works for every person.

unitMap.text: Communication, family systems, and shared decisions
coveredTopics: Disclosure; serious news context; conflict; family dynamics; caregiver distress; decisional support
Start with permission, agenda-setting, reflective listening and validation; do not promise certainty not supported by oncology information.
Family/caregiver participation is patient-defined and consent-based; document who may receive information and what the patient wants shared.
When there is disagreement, separate medical facts, values, communication barriers and unresolved safety questions; avoid coercion.

unitMap.text: Palliative care, existential distress, and end of life
coveredTopics: Meaning, dignity, grief, existential concerns, capacity interface, interdisciplinary palliative services
Palliative care is interdisciplinary support for serious illness and is not synonymous with hospice; psychiatric consultation addresses a bounded question within team care.
Explore existential, spiritual and relational suffering in the patient's own language; a wish that suffering end requires clarification rather than assumption.
Capacity questions are decision-specific and jurisdiction-dependent; a psychiatric consultation does not replace the treating team's lawful process.

unitMap.text: Caregiver, family, survivorship, and late effects
coveredTopics: Caregiver distress; survivorship; late effects; fear of recurrence; socioeconomic stressors
Transition check-ins: treatment completion, surveillance, recurrence, late effects and caregiver-role changes can create new support needs.
Survivorship planning includes practical access, cognition, sleep, relationships, work, financial stress and fear of recurrence without assuming one standardized experience.
Caregiver screening is separate from patient assessment and follows the patient's consent/privacy preferences.

unitMap.text: Interprofessional consultation and service design
coveredTopics: Consultation formulation; service models; warm handoffs; referral; documentation; QI measures
Consultation formulation: translate the referral into a focused question, relevant time course, medical context, risks, requested decision and recommendations with a named owner.
Closed-loop referral: patient consent, service match, handoff, access barrier plan and confirmation of follow-up.
Quality-improvement denominators and measures must be prespecified and privacy-protected; a process change alone does not prove improved clinical outcomes.

unitMap.text: Evidence appraisal, ethics, law, and professional practice
coveredTopics: Guideline currency; evidence hierarchy; consent and capacity; ethical/legal uncertainty; professional wellbeing; research/QI distinctions
Evidence appraisal: locate population, design, outcome, certainty, publication/version date and applicability before generalizing a recommendation.
Distinguish a clinical-program description, accreditation requirement and board-exam eligibility policy; each answers a different question.
Confidentiality, consent, capacity, research/QI distinctions and professional well-being require current institutional policy, jurisdictional law and supervision.

topicGaps: The required 36 verified specialty video hours are not met. Only 6,655 seconds (1.8486 h) of conservative transcript-time floors across two relevant free public recordings are countable; residual target gap is 34.1514 h. Exact full player runtimes were not retrievable, so these totals are minimum transcript-timestamp evidence, not full runtime claims.

Existing non-counted candidate media remain unverified for duration and/or anonymous free playback: VID-UNCCN-HOLT, VID-ASCO-ANX-2023, VID-ADDRESS-MH, VID-PSYCHPOD. UNC Mediasite pages showed public metadata/runtime but their fetched player displayed Presentation_NotAvailable; those items were not counted.

A broad public search located a small number of relevant full lectures but not a publicly measurable, freely viewable 36-hour psycho-oncology physician lecture set. APOS's 15-module Virtual Academy is 1–1.5 hours/module but access is free to APOS members and otherwise requires a $600 membership; excluded as gated. IPOS webinar archive links to events but access/duration/public playback was not verified for individual recordings.

The specialty has no independent ABPN psycho-oncology exam identified in the official sources. Parent C-L Psychiatry requirements and general Psychiatry blueprint are crosswalks, not a dedicated oncology board blueprint.

Important clinical source limitations persist: linked NCCN clinician distress guideline is v2.2024 and should be checked against current authorized version; ACGME linked PDF is 2020; ASCO 2023 recommendations apply to adults with cancer and are not a medication protocol.

Video time, authored scripts, learner study plans, institutional clinical training and clinical competence are different things. Original scripts remain scripted/planned and contribute zero verified recording hours.

medical.boardStatus: A separate ABPN Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry subspecialty certification examination exists; the official board calls the subspecialty Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry (name changed 2018). medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABPN requires primary general psychiatry certification by December 31 before the subspecialty exam year and one year of ACGME-accredited consultation-liaison psychiatry fellowship training for standard candidates, subject to all current ABPN rules. medical.programmeSourceScope: This exact packet identifies one physician clinical track at Dana-Farber. It is neither a standalone oncology residency nor a combined oncology-psychiatry board program; the C-L Psychiatry fellowship is its ACGME-accredited parent. The 2027–28 application/administrative host changes to BIDMC–VA Boston, while the cancer-facing site remains Dana-Farber and additional locations are named by the current page. Brigham affiliation is retained for current fellows only. Dana-Farber’s separately listed Supportive Oncology Research Fellowship is research-focused and excluded; Pediatric Psychosocial Oncology fellowships are psychology postdoctoral training and excluded. The APOS 15-module knowledge/skills certificate is a non-degree professional supplement with access conditions, not a physician residency, clinical fellowship or board exam. No Hopkins counterpart was included in this packet or verified as the same named clinical track.
sourceCaveats: Official Dana-Farber page is date-sensitive and describes a transition beginning July 2027; prospective structure, application deadline and sites may change.
The BIDMC page is a parent fellowship summary, not proof each general C-L rotation is a required part of the oncology track.
ACGME document fetched is a 2020 version; consult ACGME for current effective text.
The NCCN clinician guideline available at APOS is v2.2024; NCCN patient guide is 2026 and is not a clinician guideline. Verify latest clinician version before use.
NCI PDQ is reviewed/updated, not a substitute for formal diagnosis or local clinical policy.
ASCO 2023 recommendations are scoped to adults/adult survivors and specified symptom severity; not all populations or situations.
The ABPN primary psychiatry content specification is a broad examination blueprint; it is not a published C-L-specific board blueprint.
