topicGaps: The required 36 verified specialty video hours are not met. Only 6,655 seconds (1.8486 h) of conservative transcript-time floors across two relevant free public recordings are countable; residual target gap is 34.1514 h. Exact full player runtimes were not retrievable, so these totals are minimum transcript-timestamp evidence, not full runtime claims.

Existing non-counted candidate media remain unverified for duration and/or anonymous free playback: VID-UNCCN-HOLT, VID-ASCO-ANX-2023, VID-ADDRESS-MH, VID-PSYCHPOD. UNC Mediasite pages showed public metadata/runtime but their fetched player displayed Presentation_NotAvailable; those items were not counted.

A broad public search located a small number of relevant full lectures but not a publicly measurable, freely viewable 36-hour psycho-oncology physician lecture set. APOS's 15-module Virtual Academy is 1–1.5 hours/module but access is free to APOS members and otherwise requires a $600 membership; excluded as gated. IPOS webinar archive links to events but access/duration/public playback was not verified for individual recordings.

The specialty has no independent ABPN psycho-oncology exam identified in the official sources. Parent C-L Psychiatry requirements and general Psychiatry blueprint are crosswalks, not a dedicated oncology board blueprint.

Important clinical source limitations persist: linked NCCN clinician distress guideline is v2.2024 and should be checked against current authorized version; ACGME linked PDF is 2020; ASCO 2023 recommendations apply to adults with cancer and are not a medication protocol.

Video time, authored scripts, learner study plans, institutional clinical training and clinical competence are different things. Original scripts remain scripted/planned and contribute zero verified recording hours.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient starting a new chemotherapy regimen circles 7 on the Distress Thermometer and marks transport and anxiety. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Diagnose generalized anxiety disorder and begin medication.
Treat the DT score as a screening signal; clarify the marked problems in interview, assess acuity/safety, and connect to appropriate practical and mental-health supports with follow-up.
Repeat the DT only after treatment ends.
Refer only to psychiatry because every score ≥4 means psychiatric illness.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A DT score is not a diagnosis. NCCN distress workflow uses it as a trigger for further evaluation and matches referral to problems, with follow-up.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient reports sadness after a recurrence scan but maintains function, enjoys family visits, and says worry rises mainly before imaging. What additional formulation is most useful before labeling a disorder?

options.text: Assume major depression because sadness occurs in cancer.
Assess duration, functional impairment, symptom pattern, anxiety/depression criteria, medical contributors, and patient goals while normalizing understandable distress.
Avoid asking further questions because distress is expected.
Use a distress score alone to diagnose adjustment disorder.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Cancer-related distress spans ordinary adjustment to diagnosable disorders. Time course, impairment, interview and medical context distinguish; neither sadness nor the DT alone establishes a diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional oncology inpatient develops fluctuating inattention and altered sleep after a medical change. Which approach best fits C-L reasoning?

options.text: Assume adjustment disorder and start psychotherapy only.
Treat this as a potential acute delirium/medical change: assess attention and course, review medications and medical precipitants, coordinate urgent evaluation with the treating team.
Wait for a formal neuropsychological test before notifying the team.
Attribute it to depression without examining fluctuation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute fluctuating attention and cognition in a medically ill patient warrant prompt medical and medication assessment; C-L practice requires a differential and team coordination.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with cancer screens positive for depression and reports recurrent thoughts of death. Which response is best?

options.text: Infer a wish for hastened death means imminent suicidal intent.
Ask directly and sensitively about ideation, intent, plan, means, context, and protective factors; assess urgency and use institutional safety pathways with the care team.
Avoid asking because discussion increases risk.
Rely exclusively on a screening questionnaire validated in other populations.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Cancer-related existential concerns, desire for hastened death and suicidality are related but not interchangeable. Direct clinical assessment and safety escalation are required; tools supplement rather than replace assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult survivor has moderate anxiety and requests help. Which statement is most consistent with ASCO 2023?

options.text: Medication is mandatory before psychotherapy.
Offer individual or group therapy such as CBT, behavioral activation, structured activity/exercise, or supported psychosocial interventions; tailor to preference and access.
Only mindfulness is supported for moderate symptoms.
No intervention is indicated unless severe.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASCO 2023 recommends offering CBT, BA, structured physical activity/exercise, or empirically supported psychosocial interventions for moderate anxiety; patient fit, preference and access matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: During medication reconciliation, a fictional patient receiving cancer treatment has a complex regimen and new psychiatric symptoms. Which next step is most defensible?

options.text: Select a psychotropic from a generic list without checking interactions.
Review current antineoplastic/supportive drugs, medical status and interaction risks using current references; coordinate individualized shared decisions with oncology/pharmacy.
Assume all symptoms are psychological.
Stop all cancer medicines pending psychiatric review.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Psychopharmacology in medical illness requires context-specific interaction and adverse-effect review and multidisciplinary coordination; this study course cannot prescribe for a real patient.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with cancer identifies spiritual meaning and transport barriers, but no severe psychiatric symptoms. Which team response fits whole-person care?

options.text: Psychiatry must manage all listed issues.
Respond to each need through coordinated referrals, e.g., chaplaincy for spiritual support and social work/navigation for practical barriers, with the patient’s consent and follow-up.
Document the score and no further action.
Require the patient to choose a single referral.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Psychosocial care includes identifying needs, linking to appropriate supports, coordination, patient engagement and follow-up; services should match stated concerns.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with advanced cancer says “I wish this would end” but denies a plan. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: This statement alone proves active suicidal intent.
Clarify what the statement means—distress, demoralization, a wish for death, suicidal thoughts, or other needs—then assess safety and context without equating constructs.
End the interview because the patient is receiving palliative care.
Assume the statement is a normal reaction and do not follow up.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Desire for hastened death, demoralization and suicidality can overlap but are conceptually distinct; explore meaning and perform risk assessment and appropriate safety response.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient’s DT score is below a proposed threshold but reports new severe insomnia and hopelessness. What principle should guide follow-up?

options.text: A low score rules out clinically significant problems.
A screening threshold guides workflow but does not override clinical concern; assess symptoms and safety directly and arrange indicated follow-up.
Repeat the tool next year.
Refer only if the patient requests a diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening is not a rule-out diagnostic test; context and reported concerns trigger assessment irrespective of score.

practiceQuestions.stem: A program wants to evaluate its distress pathway. Which measure is a reasonable process indicator?

options.text: The program’s screening rate proves better survival.
Proportion of positive screens with documented appropriate follow-up/referral within the locally defined interval, interpreted as a process metric.
Number of patients labeled with a psychiatric diagnosis.
A copied protected patient-record sample for a class.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Closed-loop process measures can assess screen-evaluation-referral-follow-up documentation; process association is not proof of outcome causality and data must follow privacy/QI rules.

title: Acute Care Surgery and Critical Care Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (directory page covers distinct Surgical Critical Care and Acute Care Surgery fellowships)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Advanced medical/surgical foundations at MD/DO or equivalent professional level are assumed; the material is not a replacement for medical school or residency.
Learners should understand physiology, basic resuscitation terminology, statistics/evidence appraisal, anatomy, infectious disease, pharmacology and perioperative care.

Do not use for patient-specific care, unsupervised procedures, prescribing, or competency claims.

assignment.title: Fictional acute-care reasoning and evidence portfolio
assignment.instructions: For six explicitly fictional prompts covering shock, respiratory failure, trauma/transfusion, infection, neurologic change and postoperative abdominal deterioration, provide: the observations supplied; a prioritized differential; evidence or data needed; relevant current source with date and population; limitations; and what remains a supervised clinical-team decision. Link rather than copy authentic case resources. Do not use real patient records or images, board-question recollections, treatment orders or procedure instructions.
deliverables: Six 300–500 word structured case notes
One ABS exam-outline-to-unit mapping matrix
One guideline currency / update log
One media and source-rights attestation
assignment.gradingPlan: Formative rubric, 100 points: differential/physiologic reasoning 25; observation-inference separation 20; source quality and currency 20; uncertainty/special-population handling 15; communication and safety boundaries 15; citation and rights compliance 5. Red-flag unsafe/patient-specific treatment assertions require revision; no clinical sign-off.

assessment.format: Formative: 12 unit assessments, evidence appraisal, fictional case portfolio and 10 original multiple-choice questions.
assessment.passingClaim: No score predicts ABS exam performance, clinical competence, board eligibility, fellowship completion or passing. No accreditation or certification is offered.

mapping.name: Acute Care Surgery & Critical Care Fellowship (shared directory page describing two distinct offerings: one-year Surgical Critical Care fellowship; two-year Acute Care Surgery fellowship)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official BIDMC page distinguishes one one-year ACGME-accredited Surgical Critical Care fellow and one two-year Acute Care Surgery fellow per year. SCC description lists Trauma Surgical ICU, Surgical ICU, Cardiovascular Surgical ICU and Neurosciences ICU; broad organ-system and trauma-care exposures, and states SCC graduates are board eligible. ACS is described as a two-year focused ACS year followed by SCC year, with emergency general surgery/trauma and specialty rotations. Page states successful candidates for both have completed ACGME-accredited general surgery residency and are board eligible in general surgery. This public page is descriptive, not a full rotation calendar, didactic syllabus, case-log disclosure or independently verified eligibility/passing outcome. The two pathways are not one combined program or the same board credential.

unitMap.text: Scope, roles, safety, and evidence appraisal
coveredTopics: BIDMC track identity; ACGME/ABS role boundaries; team leadership; handoffs; fatigue; QI; evidence hierarchy.

unitMap.text: Initial resuscitation, shock, and perfusion reasoning
coveredTopics: Hemorrhagic, distributive, cardiogenic, obstructive shock; resuscitation endpoints; point-of-care ultrasound concepts; reassessment; monitoring.

unitMap.text: Respiratory failure, ventilation, and ARDS
coveredTopics: ARDS pathophysiology; ventilator-induced injury; oxygenation; liberation; rescue concepts; airway considerations; ventilator waveform literacy.

unitMap.text: Cardiovascular dysfunction and perioperative cardiac critical care
coveredTopics: Shock physiology; arrhythmia differential; postoperative cardiac surgery; ultrasound concepts; device/ECMO overview; monitoring limitations.

unitMap.text: Sepsis, infection, and antimicrobial stewardship
coveredTopics: Sepsis/shock definitions; source control; cultures; antimicrobial pharmacokinetics; device infection; stewardship; fungal/viral differential.

unitMap.text: Neurologic emergencies and traumatic brain injury
coveredTopics: TBI; intracranial hypertension; spinal injury; stroke/seizure; delirium; neurologic death determination; prognosis/communication.

unitMap.text: Trauma, hemorrhage, and transfusion
coveredTopics: Blunt/penetrating injury; bleeding; coagulopathy; transfusion; VTE; emergency thoracotomy indications as an exam domain only; trauma systems.

unitMap.text: Burns, thermal injury, pediatric and special populations
coveredTopics: Thermal/chemical injury; inhalation injury; pediatric emergencies; pregnancy; elderly; obesity, immunosuppression, chronic renal/pulmonary disease.

unitMap.text: Acute surgical abdomen, gastrointestinal, genitourinary and obstetric critical illness
coveredTopics: GI bleeding/ischemia/fistula/pancreatitis; postoperative leak; abdominal compartment; AKI/obstruction; pregnancy-related critical illness.

unitMap.text: Metabolic, renal, endocrine, fluid, nutrition, and pharmacology
coveredTopics: AKI/RRT concepts; acid-base and electrolytes; adrenal/pancreatic/thyroid crises; nutrition; alcohol withdrawal; altered drug PK.

unitMap.text: Transplant, immune dysfunction, organ failure, and goals of care
coveredTopics: Transplant ICU; immunology; sepsis in immunocompromised; multiorgan dysfunction; brain death; end-of-life care; organ donation.

unitMap.text: Monitoring, systems, quality, and integrated board-oriented synthesis
coveredTopics: Monitoring; statistics; administration; communication; quality; disaster preparedness; scenario-based cumulative synthesis; exam integrity.

topicGaps: The unique public recorded-media total exceeds the 36-hour video floor, but runtime does not establish the quality, currency, complete topic depth, learner competence, board readiness, or clinical capability of the recordings.

Blueprint topics with incomplete or thin focused lecture depth remain: pediatric critical illness; obstetric-gynecologic and genitourinary emergencies; acute GI syndromes beyond fistula; hematologic disorders and modern transfusion/VTE evidence; ICU pharmacokinetics and antimicrobial stewardship; biostatistics/research methods; and detailed special-population modifiers.

Some newly linked University of Florida recordings are 2025–2026 lectures, but only titles, archive dates and runtime metadata were inspected; full playback/content review of all 40 recordings was not performed.
The 2016 Brain Trauma Foundation fourth-edition guideline and older UCSD recordings are historical resources; update any clinical recommendation against current sources before use.

BIDMC does not publicly disclose the complete institutional teaching timetable, all rotation details, case volume, or course recordings. The one-year SCC and two-year ACS offerings remain distinct pathways; no independent ACS board was identified in the official sources reviewed.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardStatus.primaryBoard: American Board of Surgery (ABS) for Surgical Critical Care subspecialty certification; separate ACS fellowship does not itself establish an ACS board credential.

boardStatus.blueprintScope: The published ABS SCC CE outline weights 17 content categories and dimensions of patient care; this curriculum maps to the categories. It is not an official or validated blueprint for the BIDMC ACS fellowship.
boardStatus.eligibilityNotice: Consult ABS for current pathways and the application-year rules. BIDMC public page states successful SCC and ACS candidates will have completed ACGME-accredited general surgery residency and be board eligible in general surgery; this institutional statement is not an independent eligibility determination.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study does not create board eligibility or certification. ABS SCC certification is distinct from the BIDMC Acute Care Surgery fellowship and requires the current ABS criteria, qualifying training/cases and primary certification. No separate Acute Care Surgery board exam was found in reviewed official sources. Verify current ABS and ACGME requirements directly.

officialProgrammes.name: Acute Care Surgery & Critical Care Fellowship (shared directory page describing two distinct offerings: one-year Surgical Critical Care fellowship; two-year Acute Care Surgery fellowship)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official BIDMC page distinguishes one one-year ACGME-accredited Surgical Critical Care fellow and one two-year Acute Care Surgery fellow per year. SCC description lists Trauma Surgical ICU, Surgical ICU, Cardiovascular Surgical ICU and Neurosciences ICU; broad organ-system and trauma-care exposures, and states SCC graduates are board eligible. ACS is described as a two-year focused ACS year followed by SCC year, with emergency general surgery/trauma and specialty rotations. Page states successful candidates for both have completed ACGME-accredited general surgery residency and are board eligible in general surgery. This public page is descriptive, not a full rotation calendar, didactic syllabus, case-log disclosure or independently verified eligibility/passing outcome. The two pathways are not one combined program or the same board credential.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The task packet label matches BIDMC directory category, not a unique combined fellowship credential. Official BIDMC source confirms distinct one-year SCC and two-year ACS programmes under shared page. This curriculum is titled after the directory item but its board-aligned clinical syllabus and external lecture evidence are specifically the shared acute care surgery/surgical critical care cognitive domain; SCC CE content is mapped only to the ABS Surgical Critical Care exam, while ACS fellowship topics are mapped to no separate board exam. No Harvard/Johns Hopkins affiliation is claimed for this independent curriculum. No non-physician or research-only supplement is included.
sourceCaveats: BIDMC official programme page describes two distinct fellowships; it does not publish a complete didactic course or all rotation/case data.
BIDMC institutional “board eligible” wording is not an independent ABS eligibility ruling.
ABS SCC CE exists; no separate ACS exam/certification appeared in official sources reviewed. This is a bounded search result, not a proof that no other non-ABS credential exists.
ACGME 2025 SCC requirements require 12 months of accredited clinical training; public ACGME minimum patient categories are supervised experience and never fulfilled by this course.

Only public UCSDTraumaBurn playlist videos with observed duration are counted; all 16 were posted approximately 11–14 years before checking and are not a current practice guideline. YouTube runtime is metadata, not independent validation of clinical content.
The three procedural demonstration videos (cricothyroidotomy, chest tube insertion, diagnostic peritoneal lavage) are excluded from lecture-hour totals and do not authorize performance.
SCCM adult sepsis guideline fetch failed; its page remains linked for future review and no uninspected recommendation is attributed to it.
EAST guideline repository includes items needing update/review; date-check individual guideline. Free-to-view case pages do not imply image or patient-record reuse rights.
Human clinical review is not performed; all clinical decisions remain with qualified clinical teams and current local protocols.

Some newly linked University of Florida recordings are 2025–2026 lectures, but only titles, archive dates and runtime metadata were inspected; full playback/content review of all 40 recordings was not performed.
The 2016 Brain Trauma Foundation fourth-edition guideline and older UCSD recordings are historical resources; update any clinical recommendation against current sources before use.

BIDMC does not publicly disclose the complete institutional teaching timetable, all rotation details, case volume, or course recordings. The one-year SCC and two-year ACS offerings remain distinct pathways; no independent ACS board was identified in the official sources reviewed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trauma ICU patient has persistent hypotension after an operation. Which next reasoning step best fits safe cognitive analysis?

options.text: Assume hemorrhage because the patient is postoperative
Build a differential and seek trend, exam, bleeding, cardiac, infectious and medication data with the treating team
Start an intervention based on one blood pressure
Use the course as a substitute for bedside evaluation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Shock has multiple causes; safe reasoning starts with a differential, data and direct team evaluation rather than an automatic diagnosis or remote order. [1][2]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes the published ABS SCC exam blueprint from ACGME Milestones?

options.text: Both are exam weighting charts
Milestones are ACGME fellow assessment framework; ABS outline describes exam content categories and dimensions
Milestones alone establish board eligibility
Neither is a public source

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME states milestones are for assessment within accredited training; ABS publishes a separate SCC CE outline. [3][5][9]

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner watches a 2012 ventilation recording that recommends a specific ventilator mode. What is the best use?

options.text: Treat it as current orders
Use it as historical conceptual material, then verify claims against current evidence and supervised local protocols
Assume public access means endorsement
Copy its settings to a patient

practiceQuestions.rationale: Old lecture content may be outdated; neither recording nor self-study authorizes patient care. [10][12]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about BIDMC offerings is supported by its official page?

options.text: One 3-year integrated combined ACS-SCC residency
One-year ACGME-accredited SCC fellowship and separate two-year ACS fellowship listed together
A research-only postdoc
An ACS board-certification pathway

practiceQuestions.rationale: The page explicitly describes one-year SCC and two-year ACS fellowships as distinct offerings under one page. [1]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which examination is offered for the SCC board pathway?

options.text: No separate examination exists
ABS Surgical Critical Care Certifying Examination exists; eligibility and primary certification requirements apply
ACS fellowship exam grants certification automatically
ACGME administers an SCC board exam

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes the SCC CE as the single exam for SCC certification, with other training and primary certification requirements. [6][7][8]

practiceQuestions.stem: What can be inferred from ACGME defined-category minimums?

options.text: They are minimum experiential categories for accredited fellowship documentation, not self-study case targets
Completing questions here fulfills them
They guarantee competence
They establish BIDMC volume

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME specifies supervised experiential categories, not a course-volume substitute or proof for any individual program. [4]

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with sepsis is represented in a 2021 guideline. What is the appropriate educational caveat?

options.text: One guideline settles all contexts indefinitely
Check publication date, population, update status and local clinical context; involve the treating team
Apply a 2021 recommendation to every patient
Avoid source evaluation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guideline currency and population applicability matter; the linked 2021 source is not a patient-specific order. [16]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which practice is appropriate when studying public trauma cases?

options.text: Copy and rehost images because they are visible
Link to original case resources, review de-identification and license terms, and do not download/rehost without permission
Assume public means public domain
Use identifiable records for realism

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free viewing does not grant reproduction rights; use linked resources under their terms and never transfer patient records. [11][12]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the BIDMC page outcome claims is most defensible?

options.text: Independent course users can expect same pass rate
Institutional stated claims describe that program only and are not an individual guarantee or evidence of this course effectiveness
The claim is an ABS guarantee
It proves all ACS programs are identical

practiceQuestions.rationale: Programme marketing is scoped to institutional claims and cannot predict an individual result or independent course outcome. [1]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes procedure demonstrations in this curriculum?

options.text: They count toward lecture hours and authorize practice
Three short procedural demonstration videos were excluded from the counted lecture ledger; watching them does not confer procedural competence
They replace simulation
They are an official credential

practiceQuestions.rationale: Only selected lecture-style items with observed runtimes were counted; viewing never substitutes for supervised practice. [4]

title: Aesthetic and Reconstructive Plastic Surgery Fellowship
prerequisites: For intended level: post-plastic-surgery-residency physician learners or advanced learners studying concepts with appropriate supervision; course is not an applicant eligibility determination.
Prior knowledge of surgical anatomy, wound healing, perioperative risk, evidence appraisal and oncology/multidisciplinary care is assumed.
No operating, injecting, selecting patients, making recommendations, accessing patient records or treating patients under this course.
ABPS and Massachusetts licensure/credentialing eligibility must be checked directly with the relevant authority.
objectives: Explain the fellowship identity and distinguish it from residency, ACGME subspecialty accreditation, research posts and board certification.
Reason about aesthetic/reconstructive consultations, goals, alternatives, risk and ethical boundaries.
Organize foundational reasoning across wound healing, grafts/flaps, breast reconstruction, body contouring, facial, head/neck and trauma domains.
Use published evidence, current FDA materials and guideline status with date awareness and explicit uncertainty.
Interpret public video and image resources lawfully, without copying patient material or inferring procedural competence.
Complete original board-style cognitive practice while understanding that it is not official exam content nor a validated readiness predictor.

Apply consent, patient autonomy, equity, confidentiality, and advertising/credential-verification principles.
topics: BIDMC prerequisite is completed plastic-surgery residency; licensure and credentialing required.
HMS-hosted page describes the same one-year aesthetic fellowship, weekly rounds and three presentations/year.
ABPS requires approved residency and formal admission; fellowship cases are excluded from its oral case submission per current public page.
ACGME identifies hand and craniofacial as plastic surgery subspecialties, not aesthetic surgery.

assignment.title: Integrated reconstructive/aesthetic evidence conference memo
assignment.prompt: Using one fictional scenario (no patient identifiers, no copied images), prepare a 1,200–1,800 word consultation-and-evidence memo. State the patient-defined goal, reconstructive/aesthetic framing, missing data, alternatives including no intervention, key risks and uncertainties, multidisciplinary referrals, source dates, and why no self-study learner can select or perform an operation. Attach a 5-slide teaching outline.

rubric.excellent: Correctly distinguishes diagnosis, reconstruction/aesthetic goals, training/board status and limitations; no unsupported procedural directive.
Uses primary/authoritative sources, reports date and access/license caveat, differentiates guideline from review and identifies uncertainty.
Respectfully frames goals, options and uncertainty, autonomy, consent, equity and alternatives.
Recognizes risk, escalation, team dependencies and training boundary without inventing thresholds.
Clear and concise; claims are traceable to cited sources; no patient images or identifying material.

assignment.passStandard: Formative self-assessment only; no credential, clinical entrustment or validated pass threshold.

assessment.format: Original 10-item single-best-answer quiz, unit retrieval checks, evidence memo and self-reflection.
assessment.scoring: Rubric feedback focuses on reasoning, source fidelity, uncertainty, consent and safety. Any numeric score is a study aid, not an exam prediction.
assessment.validityNotice: Questions are original educational items, not official ABPS content and not psychometrically validated.

unitMap.text: Fellowship identity, scope, ethics, and board pathway
coveredTopics: BIDMC prerequisite is completed plastic-surgery residency; licensure and credentialing required.
HMS-hosted page describes the same one-year aesthetic fellowship, weekly rounds and three presentations/year.
ABPS requires approved residency and formal admission; fellowship cases are excluded from its oral case submission per current public page.
ACGME identifies hand and craniofacial as plastic surgery subspecialties, not aesthetic surgery.

unitMap.text: Consultation, goals, selection, and shared decisions
coveredTopics: Aesthetic intent versus reconstructive indication; expectation and outcome measures.
Risk factors, alternatives, no-procedure option, teach-back, informed consent, equity and cultural humility.
Referral/escalation for distress, unrealistic expectations, coercion, or complex comorbidity.

unitMap.text: Aesthetic surgical safety and perioperative systems
coveredTopics: Preoperative assessment, medication reconciliation, smoking/nicotine, obesity, comorbidities, anesthesia risk.
Facility accreditation, emergency readiness, checklists, postoperative monitoring and handoff.
Do not infer a specific safe outpatient threshold; local standards and clinician judgment govern.

unitMap.text: Wound biology, tissue viability, scars, grafts, and local flaps
coveredTopics: Wound-healing physiology; ischemia, infection, nutrition and nicotine as modifiers.
Graft types, donor/recipient issues, flap classification, local rearrangements, scar maturation and revision principles.
Avoid procedural instruction; conceptual reconstruction ladder and escalation only.

unitMap.text: Breast aesthetic and reconstructive decision frameworks
coveredTopics: Immediate/delayed reconstruction; implants/expanders and autologous options; multidisciplinary coordination.
High-risk factors and complication trade-offs; nipple-sparing decision is oncologic/multidisciplinary, not a cosmetic-only decision.
FDA device labeling, BIA-ALCL and other reported risks, rupture surveillance; distinguish manufacturer/FDA information from guideline recommendations.

unitMap.text: Body contouring, post-weight-loss reconstruction, and abdominoplasty
coveredTopics: Abdominoplasty, panniculectomy, body lift, thigh/brachioplasty, liposuction as curriculum topics.
Complication recognition and evidence critique; current ASPS guideline-in-progress status noted rather than fabricated recommendation.
Scar and donor-site planning; patient-reported outcomes.

unitMap.text: Facial aesthetic surgery and functional-aesthetic interfaces
coveredTopics: Rhinoplasty, blepharoplasty, brow lift, facelift/rhytidectomy, facial aging, facial proportion and functional airway/vision concerns.
Preoperative documentation and outcome measurement; no step-by-step operative instructions.
ASPS upper-eyelid guideline applies to visual-field improvement, not all cosmetic blepharoplasty.

unitMap.text: Head, neck, skin-cancer, and trauma reconstruction
coveredTopics: Facial/craniofacial trauma; skin-cancer defects; oral/head-neck defects; vascularized tissue and donor-site tradeoffs.
Free flap and microsurgical principles at conceptual level; dental/functional restoration and team interfaces.
Virtual surgical planning recording covers selected head/neck reconstruction methods but does not replace hands-on training.

unitMap.text: Breast/body perfusion, imaging, and planning evidence
coveredTopics: Reconstructive imaging choice; vascular mapping; 3D models; measurements and postoperative comparison.
Technical feasibility versus evidence of patient-important benefit; costs, access and generalizability.
No real patient images copied into this independent course.

unitMap.text: Implant complications, adverse events, and longitudinal care
coveredTopics: Capsular contracture, rupture, infection, malposition, reoperation/removal; BIA-ALCL and other FDA-described risks.
FDA labeling/decision checklist and current rupture surveillance wording; not a personalized recommendation.
Escalation and documentation; shared care with oncology and other specialists.

unitMap.text: Outcomes, evidence literacy, quality improvement, and research
coveredTopics: Study design, confounding by indication, generalizability and patient-centered outcomes.
Systematic review, evidence-based guideline and institutional educational page are distinct evidence types.
Research governance, privacy, authorship and conflicts.

unitMap.text: Integrated board-cognitive synthesis and safe referrals
coveredTopics: Cross-domain differential reasoning; timing and multidisciplinary interface; avoiding premature procedural recommendation.
Board-style single-best-answer practice is original self-assessment only, not ABPS exam content or validated predictor.
Consolidation across cosmetic and reconstructive domains; recap limits.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes the BIDMC Aesthetic & Reconstructive Plastic Surgery Fellowship?

options.text: It is a one-year clinical fellowship requiring prior plastic-surgery residency.
It is an ACGME-accredited residency that confers ABPS certification.
It is a research-only postdoctoral role with no patient-care component.
It is a separate ABMS board subspecialty.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official BIDMC page says one year and requires completion of an approved plastic-surgery residency; it makes no accreditation/board award claim.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does the official ACGME Plastic Surgery specialty page list as its plastic surgery subspecialties?

options.text: Aesthetic surgery and body contouring
Hand surgery and craniofacial plastic surgery
Breast reconstruction and microsurgery
Rhinoplasty and cosmetic facial surgery

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME lists Hand Surgery and Craniofacial Plastic Surgery. Aesthetic fellowship is a clinical institutional fellowship but is not listed as an ACGME subspecialty.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is required before ABPS examination admissibility according to its public page?

options.text: Completion of this one-year aesthetic fellowship alone
A Final Confirmation Letter after the Board reviews required training registration and application
A pass on an aesthetic fellowship exam
Completion of three aesthetic cases during fellowship

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPS states candidate needs a Final Confirmation Letter; admissibility and requirements are Board-controlled.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellow asks whether fellowship cases may be submitted for ABPS oral-examination case submission. Best answer?

options.text: Yes, all fellowship cases count automatically.
No; ABPS says fellowship training delays oral admissibility and its nine-month oral case submission cannot include fellowship cases.
Only aesthetic cases count.
There is a separate ABPS aesthetic exam.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABPS page explicitly says fellowship cases cannot be included in the oral examination case submission; do not infer a separate aesthetic exam.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which factor set is most appropriate for a conceptual breast reconstruction risk discussion?

options.text: Only patient age
Medical/physiologic/anatomic and oncologic context, treatment timing, risk factors, patient preferences, and multidisciplinary input
Implant preference alone
A fixed universally safe BMI threshold

practiceQuestions.rationale: The high-risk review stresses multiple interacting conditions and judicious evaluation; no universal candidacy or threshold is supplied here.

practiceQuestions.stem: A freely accessible figure in an open-access clinical paper may be copied into course materials without checking anything else.

options.text: True; free viewing always grants reuse rights.
False; check article and figure-specific license and attribution, and do not assume patient-image consent/de-identification.
True if the patient name is not shown.
True for educational use in any jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-view is not blanket reuse permission. Article license and third-party figure credits apply; patient privacy/consent also require care.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which distinction between a skin graft and a flap is most accurate at a high level?

options.text: A graft transfers tissue with its own intact vascular pedicle; flap relies only on recipient-bed inosculation.
A graft depends on recipient-bed revascularization; a flap transfers tissue with an associated blood supply.
Both have identical vascular biology.
A flap is always free tissue transfer.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Basic reconstructive principle: graft survival depends on recipient bed, while flap includes transferred vascular supply; detailed choices require supervised training.

practiceQuestions.stem: What should a learner do with current implant surveillance recommendations?

options.text: Use an old interval from any lecture regardless of date.
Check current FDA and device-specific labeling; distinguish educational material from personalized clinical advice.
Promise implants are lifetime devices.
Recommend the same imaging schedule to every patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA material and manufacturer labeling can change; current page extraction was unavailable in this research session, so check direct source and avoid outdated intervals.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient requests an elective appearance change and describes marked distress and pressure from another person. What is the safest educational next reasoning step?

options.text: Immediately recommend a procedure.
Clarify patient-led goals, assess capacity/expectations and coercion, discuss alternatives/no procedure, and refer/escalate when appropriate.
Use social-media before/after photos as consent.
Dismiss the person as unsuitable based on a label.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Shared decision-making, autonomy and safe assessment come before procedure selection; no diagnosis is inferred in this fictional vignette.

practiceQuestions.stem: What can virtual 3D planning establish by itself?

options.text: It proves an operation is indicated and guarantees outcome.
It can support visualization/planning, but does not independently establish indication, benefit or competence.
It replaces direct clinical assessment.
It eliminates bias and resource limitations.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The systematic review describes planning uses and limitations; modality selection is context dependent and evidence/generalizability remain qualified.

topicGaps: Two unique Utah recordings are now counted: 53:18 from 2024-11-06 and 01:06:38 from the single 2024-03-27 session; total 01:59:56 (7,196 seconds; 1.9989 hours). The March session contains two burn/critical-care fellow talks and is counted once, not as two videos.
The verified video floor remains short by 34.0011 hours. Target minutes and authored scripts are production plans, not rendered or verified media and do not close this gap.

Open-duration-verified professional video remains particularly sparse for inhalation injury, pediatric and geriatric burn reasoning, wound infection/analgesia, operative excision/coverage and reconstruction, nutrition/sepsis/organ support, safeguarding, disaster operations, and integrated board-style case reasoning.

ACS H.O.P.E. acute-burn webinar and a University of Saskatchewan burn rehabilitation webinar are relevant public-page candidates, but direct unrestricted playback and/or exact runtime could not be observed; neither is counted.

The 2024 ABA burn-shock guideline is population-limited to adults with ≥20% TBSA during the first 48 hours; it is taught as evidence appraisal, not patient dosing. The 2018 inhalation-injury review and 2020 broad burn review are dated and do not replace current specialist guidance.

No complete official Hopkins didactic inventory, rotation schedule, or public fellowship lecture-hour disclosure was found. No burn-specific board blueprint or examination was identified; ABS Surgical Critical Care certification remains a distinct route with separate eligibility requirements.

Five original scripts now provide source-grounded teaching inputs across assessment, inhalation-injury reasoning, burn-shock guideline appraisal, electrical-injury reasoning, and rehabilitation handoff. They are scripted only and do not constitute clinical training or the 36-hour target.

medical.boardStatus: As checked 2026-10-07, no separate burn-surgery specialty board examination/certificate was identified in the Johns Hopkins programme description or ABS certification pages reviewed. ABS does have a distinct Surgical Critical Care certifying examination, but its route requires qualifying accredited SCC training and primary surgery certification. Do not imply the Hopkins Burn Surgery Fellowship by itself is ACGME-accredited SCC training or confers SCC exam eligibility. ABA FABA is a professional fellowship recognition and is not represented as a board exam. No burn-specific board blueprint/weights were found.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: The current Johns Hopkins listing calls the fellowship “Non-Standard,” describes 1 or 2 years, and states that a position is available to physicians board eligible/certified in plastic or general surgery, or those who have completed three years of general surgery training; international medical graduates may be considered with appropriate qualifications and ECFMG certification. This is the institution’s published statement, not a guarantee of eligibility, selection, accreditation, licensure, or board access. ABS SCC eligibility is separate and depends on ABS requirements in effect at application, including qualifying accredited SCC training and primary certification. Confirm directly with the programme and board.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet identifies one physician clinical fellowship. It is an actual institutional burn surgery fellowship, not merely a generic directory category, research-only postdoc or non-physician course. Preserve Hopkins’ “Burn Surgery Fellowship” wording and its “Non-Standard” accreditation label. No Harvard-affiliated variant is in this MED-199 packet. A burn-focused clinical fellowship is distinct from ACGME SCC. Rotating regional residents are not separate burn fellowships. No separate burn-surgery board exam was identified; ABS SCC board examination is a distinct pathway. ABA FABA, nursing CBRN, therapist BT-C and ABLS products are not physician burn-surgery board certification.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins official directory states “Accrediting Body: Non-Standard.” Do not imply an ACGME-accredited burn fellowship or assume ACGME-SCC board eligibility. The ACGME public directory is dynamic and not independently searched for a specific Hopkins SCC program in this task.

ABS has a distinct SCC examination, but SCC-specific ACGME training and primary certification requirements apply. No burn-specific examination or blueprint was identified on reviewed official pages. Board/eligibility rules are date-sensitive and must be reconfirmed.

Counted time includes one 53:18 Utah General Surgery Grand Rounds recording, verified from official player display and linked MP4 metadata, counted once. It is not institutional Hopkins lecture content. No other candidates are counted.
A true 35.1117-hour gap remains. Plans and scripts are not completed/rendered films. Unknown-duration/media-access candidates remain outside all totals. No foundation/supplemental hours are counted.

ABA referral material advises consultation and is not a substitute for professional judgment. The 2024 ABA shock guideline is scoped to adults with burns ≥20% TBSA during first 48 hours; avoid extrapolating it to different populations.
The 2020 review is broad, open reading but older; it is not a current standalone protocol. ABA guideline catalog includes older literature; verify currentness at source.

Case report de-identification/consent assertions are those reported by article authors and were not independently audited. Free-to-view does not authorize reuse. No image or record is copied/rehosted.

Human clinical review is not performed. This independent education grants no institutional affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, procedure competence, certification or passing guarantee.

Open-duration-verified professional video remains particularly sparse for inhalation injury, pediatric and geriatric burn reasoning, wound infection/analgesia, operative excision/coverage and reconstruction, nutrition/sepsis/organ support, safeguarding, disaster operations, and integrated board-style case reasoning.

ACS H.O.P.E. acute-burn webinar and a University of Saskatchewan burn rehabilitation webinar are relevant public-page candidates, but direct unrestricted playback and/or exact runtime could not be observed; neither is counted.

The 2024 ABA burn-shock guideline is population-limited to adults with ≥20% TBSA during the first 48 hours; it is taught as evidence appraisal, not patient dosing. The 2018 inhalation-injury review and 2020 broad burn review are dated and do not replace current specialist guidance.

No complete official Hopkins didactic inventory, rotation schedule, or public fellowship lecture-hour disclosure was found. No burn-specific board blueprint or examination was identified; ABS Surgical Critical Care certification remains a distinct route with separate eligibility requirements.

Five original scripts now provide source-grounded teaching inputs across assessment, inhalation-injury reasoning, burn-shock guideline appraisal, electrical-injury reasoning, and rehabilitation handoff. They are scripted only and do not constitute clinical training or the 36-hour target.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult educational vignette describes full-thickness thermal burns and no other known injuries. Which statement best aligns with current ABA referral guidance?

options.text: Full-thickness injuries warrant immediate consultation with consideration of transfer to a burn center.
Only burns exceeding 20% TBSA warrant consultation.
Full-thickness burn can be managed without specialist input if pain is low.
The guideline is a substitute for professional judgment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABA lists full-thickness burns for immediate consultation with consideration for transfer; guidance supports, not replaces, judgment and local resources.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner uses an adult Rule of Nines on an infant to estimate TBSA. Which critique is most appropriate?

options.text: The rule is equally accurate at all ages.
Use an age-appropriate Lund–Browder chart; child proportions differ from adults.
Count superficial erythema as burn TBSA in every case.
TBSA cannot be estimated clinically.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABA referral material notes that Rule of Nines is most accurate for adults and age-adjusted Lund–Browder estimates are preferred in children.

practiceQuestions.stem: The 2024 ABA adult burn-shock guideline primarily addresses which population/time window?

options.text: All pediatric burns for the first 7 days.
Adults with burns ≥20% TBSA during the first 48 hours.
Minor burns managed as outpatients.
Electrical burns regardless of TBSA only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PubMed abstract defines adults with ≥20% TBSA burns and acute resuscitation in the first 48 hours; applicability should not be extrapolated without qualification.

practiceQuestions.stem: A question asks if high-dose vitamin C should routinely be added as an adjunct in burn-shock resuscitation according to the 2024 ABA CPG. Which response is correct?

options.text: Strong recommendation for all patients.
Strong recommendation for every child.
The panel could not make a recommendation on high-dose vitamin C.
It is the only recommended fluid.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline abstract states insufficient evidence to make recommendations on high-dose vitamin C and several other adjuncts; this is not a recommendation for or against use in a specific patient.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has smoke exposure in an enclosed space, facial flash burns and singed nasal hairs, but normal initial oxygen saturation and chest radiograph. What is the most defensible educational inference?

options.text: Inhalation injury is excluded.
The findings support consultation/assessment; normal early tests alone do not exclude evolving inhalation injury.
A specific airway procedure is automatically indicated.
The patient must have carbon monoxide poisoning.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABA lists facial flash burns/singed hairs/smoke exposure as potential signs warranting consultation; the review notes normal oxygenation/chest radiographs do not exclude inhalation injury. Clinical decisions require qualified care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A published high-voltage electrical-injury case report describes occult deep abdominal injury and limb compromise. How should it be used in this course?

options.text: As a universal treatment protocol.
As an authentic, linked teaching case illustrating the potential for occult injury, without copying its images or making it a template.
As proof that all electrical injuries require the same operation.
As an official ABS exam item.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The open case report illustrates possible severe internal injury after high-voltage exposure; a case report is not generalizable treatment authority. Article states open CC BY 4.0, but no image/record is copied or rehosted.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which label does Johns Hopkins Medicine currently show on its official Burn Surgery Fellowship directory entry under “Accrediting Body”?

options.text: ACGME Accredited
American Board of Burn Surgery
Non-Standard
ACGME-International

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official directory entry lists “Non-Standard”; therefore this record does not claim it is an ACGME-accredited burn fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about certification best matches ABS pages reviewed in October 2026?

options.text: ABS awards a stand-alone burn surgery board certificate after any Hopkins burn fellowship.
ABS has a Surgical Critical Care certifying exam, but its pathway requires eligible SCC training and primary certification; that is separate from the Hopkins non-standard burn fellowship.
No separate SCC exam exists.
Any burn course grants SCC exam eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes a distinct SCC CE and certification pathway, requiring qualifying training and primary certification. Hopkins labels its fellowship non-standard; no separate burn surgery examination was identified on reviewed board pages.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the best characterization of the 53:18 Utah Grand Rounds video listed in the curriculum?

options.text: Official Johns Hopkins fellowship lecture.
Public, free University of Utah general-surgery grand rounds; one external burn-topic lecture, counted once.
36 hours of burn fellowship training.
A surgical procedure credential.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official Utah page confirms the video, presenter and date; MediaSpace displays 53:18. It is not a Johns Hopkins lecture, training credit or competence attestation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A student completes the videos and passes the course’s original question set. What does that establish?

options.text: Board eligibility and procedure competence.
ACGME fellowship completion.
Only formative performance on independent educational material; it does not establish clinical competence, eligibility or certification.
A passing probability validated by ABS.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Independent self-study cannot substitute for supervised accredited training, board requirements or observed competence; the questions are original and unvalidated.

assignment.title: Heart-Team case portfolio: evidence, uncertainty and longitudinal context
assignment.prompt: Prepare three concise, source-cited educational case analyses: (1) a learner-constructed fictional valve referral; (2) the linked published aortic-valve case report, separating reported facts from your interpretation; and (3) a selected publicly accessible congenital or aortic case that you link to without copying images. For each give a problem representation, differential/decision questions, what data are missing, applicable current guideline source and date, relevant multidisciplinary participants, psychosocial/longitudinal considerations, and limits of inference. Do not prescribe for an actual patient, publish patient records, copy or redistribute images, or give procedural instructions.

rubric.criterion: Clinical reasoning and differential with uncertainty
Evidence appraisal, guideline date and authority/type
Safety, escalation, ethics, privacy and rights compliance

assignment.limitations: Educational exercise only; not validated, not clinical performance assessment, and not an exam predictor.

assessment.format: Twelve low-stakes formative case memos, 10 original single-best-answer practice questions, and one evidence-synthesis capstone; suggested review threshold 80% is for self-check only.
assessment.blueprintAlignment: ABTS publicly describes certification pathway/exam sequence, not a detailed open public blueprint sufficiently granular to quantify here. Units are aligned thematically to adult cardiac, general thoracic, congenital cardiac, critical care and professional practice domains; no numerical exam-weight claims are made.
assessment.limitations: Original questions are not official ABTS content, psychometrically validated, predictive of certification, or a clinical competency instrument.

studyHours.plan: Suggested self-study plan: 12 units × 5 hours (60 planned learner hours across lectures, readings, case analysis and assessment), plus the currently verified public video ledger stated separately. Learner hours are a plan, not observed media or clinical training.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins Hospital / Johns Hopkins School of Medicine
mapping.name: Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program (three-year post-surgical-residency programme; adult cardiac, congenital cardiac and thoracic rotations)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a three-year programme following surgical residency: year 1 adult cardiac/congenital/thoracic rotations; year 2 thoracic and adult cardiac, including advanced heart/lung failure therapies such as MCS, ECMO and transplant, with elective opportunities; year 3 chief resident in adult cardiac surgery, with thoracic-service time available for strong thoracic interests. It is broader than a cardiac-only programme. Public sources do not establish every didactic or individualized rotation. Official program says it accepts NRMP applications.

mapping.name: MGH Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program — cardiac track; conventional and 4+3 pathways (separate thoracic track also exists)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page states separate cardiac and thoracic tracks and conventional and 4+3 pathways; weekly didactics cover both cardiac and thoracic topics, while clinical rotations are tailored. Cardiac track descriptions include thoracic exposure, structural heart, Boston Children’s congenital experience, MCS/ICU and broad adult cardiac disease. Do not merge with Hopkins or Brigham variants.

mapping.institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital / Boston Children’s Hospital (Harvard Medical School-affiliated)
mapping.name: BWH Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency — two-year traditional cardiac track; distinct six-year integrated cardiac track also listed
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page distinguishes two-year traditional and six-year integrated thoracic surgery residencies, each with cardiac versus thoracic tracks. Cardiac track includes first-year cardiac/thoracic rotations and congenital cardiac exposure at Boston Children’s; integrated programme begins from medical school with general surgery components. It states programs prepare for ABTS certification and describes ACGME accreditation. Preserve independent vs integrated and cardiac vs thoracic variants; do not merge research/non-ACGME fellows.

topicGaps: No external lecture-hour deficit against the 36-hour floor remains in the observed ledger; the surplus is not a claim of comprehensive blueprint coverage or clinical competence.

Coverage remains adult-cardiac weighted. The additions improve CPB, adult congenital, MCS/transplant, perioperative AKI, selected valve and thoracic-interface topics, but there is still no full public ABTS topic-weight blueprint or complete procedure-level curriculum.

The open lecture sample cannot substitute for structured instruction in neonatal congenital operations, detailed postoperative hemodynamic management, detailed perfusion practice, endocarditis, pulmonary hypertension, coronary evidence updates, operative decision-making across uncommon lesions, or supervised clinical training. Use current specialist-reviewed sources for these areas.

No private institutional didactics were accessed. Exact individualized rotations and curricula beyond the public institutional descriptions remain unavailable; player playback and continued availability of public videos must be rechecked before use.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician residency (cardiothoracic/thoracic surgery with adult cardiac emphasis; institutional cardiac tracks preserved)
boardNames: American Board of Thoracic Surgery (ABTS) — Thoracic Surgery initial certification: Part I (Written) followed by Part II (Oral), after approved pathway/training and other requirements.

ABTS — Congenital Cardiac Surgery subspecialty certification has its own distinct Part I (Written) and Part II (Oral) examination sequence; it is not presumed included in primary thoracic certification. Applicants must verify current pathway eligibility directly with ABTS.
medical.boardStatus: A distinct ABTS thoracic surgery certificate exists and ABTS describes a written Part I and oral Part II sequence for approved candidates. Congenital Cardiac Surgery has a distinct ABTS subspecialty certification with separate written and oral examinations. The ABTS page checked 2026-10-07 states that trainees starting on/after July 1, 2023 must complete two consecutive years of ACGME training in one programme and 150 major cases (minimum 50 in year one) for the congenital subspecialty pathway; current official requirements control. Board pathways and examination details rechecked 2026-10-07; recheck before applying.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational self-study does not confer ACGME/RCPSC training, ABTS eligibility, ABTS certification, state licensure, operative exposure, case logs, procedural competence, or completion of medical/surgical prerequisites. ABTS pathways require accredited training and other current requirements including unrestricted licensure. No passing guarantee.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins Hospital / Johns Hopkins School of Medicine
officialProgrammes.name: Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program (three-year post-surgical-residency programme; adult cardiac, congenital cardiac and thoracic rotations)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a three-year programme following surgical residency: year 1 adult cardiac/congenital/thoracic rotations; year 2 thoracic and adult cardiac, including advanced heart/lung failure therapies such as MCS, ECMO and transplant, with elective opportunities; year 3 chief resident in adult cardiac surgery, with thoracic-service time available for strong thoracic interests. It is broader than a cardiac-only programme. Public sources do not establish every didactic or individualized rotation. Official program says it accepts NRMP applications.

officialProgrammes.name: MGH Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program — cardiac track; conventional and 4+3 pathways (separate thoracic track also exists)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page states separate cardiac and thoracic tracks and conventional and 4+3 pathways; weekly didactics cover both cardiac and thoracic topics, while clinical rotations are tailored. Cardiac track descriptions include thoracic exposure, structural heart, Boston Children’s congenital experience, MCS/ICU and broad adult cardiac disease. Do not merge with Hopkins or Brigham variants.

officialProgrammes.institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital / Boston Children’s Hospital (Harvard Medical School-affiliated)
officialProgrammes.name: BWH Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency — two-year traditional cardiac track; distinct six-year integrated cardiac track also listed
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page distinguishes two-year traditional and six-year integrated thoracic surgery residencies, each with cardiac versus thoracic tracks. Cardiac track includes first-year cardiac/thoracic rotations and congenital cardiac exposure at Boston Children’s; integrated programme begins from medical school with general surgery components. It states programs prepare for ABTS certification and describes ACGME accreditation. Preserve independent vs integrated and cardiac vs thoracic variants; do not merge research/non-ACGME fellows.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Packet names the Johns Hopkins cardiothoracic residency page. Search of official Harvard-affiliated programme pages identified MGH cardiac track and BWH/Boston Children’s two-year traditional cardiac and six-year integrated cardiac tracks. Exact variants are preserved. Separate thoracic tracks are not recast as cardiac tracks; BWH’s non-ACGME research/clinical fellow positions are excluded. No separate Johns Hopkins cardiac-only specialty was found. Public institutional pages identify programme offerings, not full private curricula or individual eligibility. ACGME has separate independent and integrated thoracic surgery requirements; clinical institutional tracks must not be conflated with directory categories or with the board.
sourceCaveats: The packet’s “Cardiac Surgery Residency” heading is broader than the official Johns Hopkins name: its official clinical programme is Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency with adult cardiac, congenital cardiac and thoracic rotations.
ACGME 2026 requirements page was published with effective date 2026-07-01, checked on 2026-10-07. ABTS rules may change; verify immediately before applying.
Hopkins operative table is explicitly one representative 2020 graduating chief and is not a population estimate, minimum, or promise.

Programme track availability, accreditation, curricula and board eligibility must be confirmed directly with each institution and the relevant accreditor/board. No public page reviewed substantiates all individualized curriculum details.

Video durations were publicly observed from playlist metadata on 2026-10-07 with yt-dlp; count only unique selected lecture recordings. This does not constitute clinical quality review, current guideline validation, or confirmed future playback. Check access live before assigning.
Substantial gaps remain. Original clip plans are plans, not completed, rendered, uploaded or ready videos.
Clinical images and real patient records are not copied. Free-to-view is not a general reuse license. Human clinical review was not performed.

ABTS congenital subspecialty page checked 2026-10-07: from July 1, 2023 entrants, two consecutive years of ACGME training in one program and specified major-case experience are stated as congenital subspecialty prerequisites; verify the current booklet and pathway details directly with ABTS.

The open lecture sample cannot substitute for structured instruction in neonatal congenital operations, detailed postoperative hemodynamic management, detailed perfusion practice, endocarditis, pulmonary hypertension, coronary evidence updates, operative decision-making across uncommon lesions, or supervised clinical training. title: Colorectal Surgery Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (independent self-study curriculum; not fellowship training)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.intendedLevel: Senior general-surgery resident, colorectal surgery fellow, board-certified surgeon refreshing knowledge, or medically trained learner with equivalent foundations; not a novice procedural-skills course.
recommendedPrerequisites: Completed core medical education and general-surgery foundations; familiarity with abdominal/pelvic anatomy, physiology, pathology, imaging, perioperative care and evidence appraisal.
For board-oriented use, familiarity with ABS qualifying-exam knowledge and current professional practice; this course cannot substitute for either.
notFor: Independent procedural performance or patient-specific treatment decisions
Demonstrating competence, case numbers, credentialing or board eligibility
Replacing supervised clinical education or institutional rotations

objectives: Integrate anatomy, physiology, pathology, endoscopy, radiology and perioperative reasoning across colon, rectum and anus.
Construct a differential and identify time-critical risks for common colorectal presentations without substituting a self-study algorithm for specialist judgement.
Explain multidisciplinary options for colon and rectal neoplasia, IBD, diverticular disease, anorectal disease, pelvic-floor disorders and emergencies, including uncertainty and patient preferences.
Analyze surgical-outcome evidence, guidelines and complications; distinguish board domains from ACGME training requirements and institutional programme claims.
Prepare structured written rationales and oral-case discussions aligned to the broad publicly described ABCRS written and oral examination scope.

assignment.title: Colorectal MDT and oral-case portfolio
deliverables: Three fictional case write-ups: colon cancer, rectal cancer and IBD/benign disease; label all fictional facts.
One diagnostic-imaging/pathology synthesis using linked public cases only; no patient record or image copied.
A short critical appraisal of one current guideline/research source and a 5-minute oral case presentation.
assignment.safety: Educational scenarios only; not validated board content or patient-care instructions. No real-patient data or unlicensed image copies.

assessment.format: 12 unit checks, 10 original practice questions, three fictional cases, an evidence appraisal and oral-case presentation.
assessment.passingStandard: No board-passing threshold is asserted. Use a local instructor or qualified clinician to review clinical reasoning before relying on it; human clinical review of this curriculum has not been performed.
assessment.limits: Questions are original educational items, not official or recalled ABCRS/ABS questions and not validated predictors of examination performance. Written/oral board format descriptions are from ABCRS primary sources.

studyHours.planBreakdown: Self-study plan, not clinical training time: 36 hours lecture viewing target (currently only the verified actual amounts below), 72 hours reading/guideline comparison, 36 hours case reasoning, 24 hours question review and 12 hours portfolio/oral practice. topicGaps: Only 4.0664 verified hours are specialty-specific, against the 36-hour specialty-video floor (31.9336 hours remain). Across all categories, the unique observed public ledger totals 6.6869 hours; 1.1425 foundation hours and 1.4781 supplement hours are separately reported and are not substituted for specialty hours.

New public full-video leads were found on diverticulitis controversies, colon cancer operative standards, and hereditary polyposis; page extraction did not expose exact total player runtimes for these new leads, so they remain uncounted pending duration verification.

Source-backed original scripts address basic reasoning in anatomy/diagnostic framing, diverticulitis evidence appraisal, colon cancer MDT synthesis, and rectal cancer staging/function. They are planned scripts, not rendered or observed video; they contribute zero verified hours.

Insufficient verified lecture coverage remains for anatomy and physiology, endoscopy/pathology, hereditary risk, Crohn/UC decisions and pouch disease, anorectal/pelvic-floor disorders, metastatic disease, emergencies, ostomy and QI. Readings and scripted teaching can support self-study but cannot be translated into video hours.
No numeric ABCRS topic-weight blueprint was identified in the reviewed official material; domain mapping remains broad, not percentage-weighted.
Public BIDMC programme pages describe selected exposures and approximate programme case volume, not its internal lecture curriculum or guaranteed learner experience.

boardNames: American Board of Colon and Rectal Surgery (ABCRS)
American Board of Surgery (ABS)
medical.boardStatus: Colon and Rectal Surgery has a distinct ABCRS certification pathway and separate written Part I and oral Part II examinations. ABS certification is separately required before ABCRS oral Part II. ACGME accreditation governs fellowship programme standards, not this independent course. The ABCRS written domain is described broadly as colon and rectal surgery, including radiology, pathology and pertinent basic science; no verified public numeric topic-weight blueprint was identified.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational curriculum does not create ABCRS or ABS board eligibility. ABCRS eligibility requires completion of an ACGME-accredited colon and rectal surgery residency after an approved general surgical residency leading to ABS certification, current unrestricted medical licensure, ABS qualifying examination before ABCRS written examination, and ABS certification before ABCRS oral examination. The Board determines individual eligibility. Check current ABCRS rules directly.

ABCRS is a separate colon and rectal surgery board with written and oral exams. ABS is a distinct board and prerequisite. ABCRS broad domains are stated, but no accessible numeric topic-weight blueprint was verified.
Current ACGME page lists the requirements effective July 1, 2026. ACGME accreditation is programme recognition, not individual certification. No direct ACGME compliance audit was performed.

Clinical sources include NCI PDQs last updated 2025-02-12, ASCRS/SAGES ERAS 2022, and other sources with varying dates. Check for later guideline revisions before clinical use; board rules and exam schedules also change.

Public YouTube and institutional video player pages expose duration and full-video controls. Videos were not downloaded. Link-only study access does not authorize embedding/reposting. One 2021 postoperative lecture is industry sponsored and supplement-only; a 2016 Utah lecture and 2016-presented ERAS lecture are dated.

ASCRS public page advertises a no-cost Toolkit but its terms limit use and prohibit public display or transfer; specific content may require a subscription. No ASCRS U recording is counted. ACS course pages require registration/payment, so not counted. ISUCRS library has free surgical videos but not a complete verified runtime ledger; no series-wide hours counted.

Radiopaedia case is authentic published imaging, but the public metadata does not independently establish formal de-identification/consent provenance. No case images or patient records are copied, stored, or embedded; direct links only.

This independent course has no Harvard, BIDMC, Johns Hopkins, ACGME, ABCRS, ABS, ACS, ASCRS or SAGES affiliation or endorsement. Human clinical review is not performed. No accreditation, licensure, board eligibility, guaranteed pass, procedure competence, clinical case volume or patient-care authorization is claimed.
